tweets.nap-17961106-168: Soldiers, I am displeased: no courage, no discipline, no constancy. No ground rallied you; panic scattered you where a handful could have stood. I expect better of my army.
tweets.nap-17961109-50: I arrived at Verona day before yesterday, my dearest love. Though fatigued I am very well; much prospered, and I love you always passionately. I mount my horse. I embrace you a thousand times.
tweets.nap-17961113-51: I do not love you at all; on the contrary, I detest you. You are a naughty woman, very crooked, very unfeeling, very ungenerous. Tu es une vilaine, bien gauche, bien bete, bien cendrillon. You do not write me at all. My heart is torn by your silence.
tweets.nap-17961124-52: I hope very soon, my sweet love, to be in your arms. I love you most passionately. All goes well. Wurmser was beaten yesterday under Mantua. There is nothing wanted by your husband but the love of Josephine, in order to be happy.
tweets.nap-17961128-53: I have received the express which Berthier had dispatched from Genoa. You had not time to write me. I feel it sensibly. Your letters are my life; without them I am incomplete.
tweets.nap-17961201-19: The army of General Alvinzi is on the Brenta and in the Tyrol, and that of the Republic along the Adige. Mantua is invested with the greatest care. You will see by the Emperor's letter that Wurmser must be in extremis. The army returns you sent are full of errors.
tweets.nap-17970201-163: My savants reaped nobly at Ravenna, Rimini, Pesaro, Ancona, Loretto, Perugia; all comes straight to Paris.
tweets.nap-17970202-26: I mantua's imperial garrison marches out the main gate with war's honours, drums beating, colours flying. Answer: granted. The siege ends; Mantua is ours.
tweets.nap-17970203-27: I brigadier rusca commands all romagna, spreading conquest further. The revolutionary flag advances.
tweets.nap-17970203-28: I have sent Leclerc to Russi today; Ravenna should be reassured by the peaceful terms.
tweets.nap-17970204-29: I have ordered a year’s provisions for 12,000 men and 2,000 horses at Mantua, including medicines.
tweets.nap-17970206-30: I victor's vanguard to sinigaglia tomorrow. The offensive does not pause.
tweets.nap-17970213-01: I receive no letters from you. I do not doubt that you love me no longer. I have sent you newspapers and several letters. I leave this very moment to pass the mountains. As soon as matters are settled I will send for you to come to me. It is the dearest wish of my heart.
tweets.nap-17970302-31: I cut every house harming the fortress's defence. The ramparts must be clear.
tweets.nap-17970305-32: Answering your letter on Corsica's military state. The island's defence concerns me.
tweets.nap-17970305-33: I mantuans declare all Austrian stores. Nothing of the enemy's shall be hidden.
tweets.nap-17970306-34: I have issued orders for Mantua on demolitions, religious communities, and compensation.
tweets.nap-17970321-164: An unjust terror has preceded the French army; we have not come to conquer you, or to change your customs or your religion. The French Republic is the friend of all nations. Perdition to those kings who are mad enough to do it battle.
tweets.nap-17970416-21: I send you by General Leclerc some interesting despatches concerning the situation of the army and the negotiations commenced. In passing through Germany Leclerc will observe enemy movements and inform Generals Moreau and Hoche on reaching the Rhine.
tweets.nap-17970502-35: I am enclosing the Venice manifesto. Print 1,000 copies and circulate them.
tweets.nap-17970506-36: I am sending all Venetian soldier-prisoners to France.
tweets.nap-17970506-37: Your letter and prints received, Bishop; the motto displeased me. The Church must align with the Republic.
tweets.nap-17970506-38: I need the Corsican gendarmerie paid; unpaid troops have risen, and order must be restored.
tweets.nap-17970506-39: I livorno's garrison embarks for Corsica within days. Reinforcements sail for the troubled isle.
tweets.nap-17970514-22: You will find inclosed the ratification of the Emperor to the preliminary treaty. The plenipotentiary regretted the treaty not on parchment, seals not larger. I agree; parchment ought to be used for documents meant to be preserved.
tweets.nap-17970702-40: I enclosed: Lombardy independence proclamation. The New Republic is declared.
tweets.nap-17970702-41: I gallo showed Naples powers: Elba offered for the Levant isles. Diplomatic exchanges continue.
tweets.nap-17970703-42: Enclosed intercepted Antraigues mail. The spy's correspondence is in my hands.
tweets.nap-17970703-43: I have ordered the Pavia mobile column to march and spend the night at Milan.
tweets.nap-17970705-44: I impatiently await the Venice marine inspection. The fleet must be ready.
tweets.nap-17970714-23: Soldiers, today rings the anniversary of our revolution's great day. Before you stand the names of comrades fallen for liberty; they set you a shining example. You owe yourselves to the Republic, to thirty million Frenchmen, and to glory.
tweets.nap-17970726-24: I have received your letter. The music for which you ask is being copied in the various towns of Italy. I shall take the greatest care to enrich the conservatory.
tweets.nap-17970801-25: Attempts have been made to disturb your Royal Highness, and to invent motives for dispute between you and the French Republic.
tweets.nap-17970902-45: Glad His Majesty ordered the division reorganized. The army improves by your command.
tweets.nap-17970902-46: I want Rome pressed to recognize the Cisalpine Republic.
tweets.nap-17970902-47: I have ordered the Fifth Line regiment to leave Venice for Tortona.
tweets.nap-17970903-48: I forwarding the finance minister's letter; print it. The accounts must be public.
tweets.nap-17970913-165: I think that henceforward the maxim of the Republic should be never to abandon Corfu, Zante, etc.
tweets.nap-17971101-26: Today we proceeded to exchange the ratifications of the treaty of Campo Formio. All the members of the Congress have arrived and have paid me a visit. The king of Sweden has sent the Baron de Fersen as his ambassador.
tweets.nap-17971117-169: Cisalpine Republic, we gave you liberty; guard it. To deserve your fate make only wise, honourable laws and enforce them hard. Spread knowledge, honour religion. I trust your future to you.
tweets.nap-17971210-01: I to be free, the French people had kings to fight. The Directory must now secure the peace won by the sword.
tweets.nap-17971213-03: I have just received your works. Your pen is a paintbrush. The writer who paints nature serves the Republic.
tweets.nap-17971226-04: The votes of the distinguished men of the Institut honor me. Before being their equal I shall long be their schoolboy. Science and glory walk the same path.
tweets.nap-17980106-05: Months ago I sent two deputies to the Maniots. The Greek allies await my direction.
tweets.nap-17980111-07: I received, my dear general, the letters you wrote me. The honor of taking Rome is reserved to you. The eternal city falls to French arms.
tweets.nap-17980114-08: Enclosed, Citizen minister, the notes you asked of me. The diplomatic papers are ready.
tweets.nap-17980116-09: By the latest Levant letters, our commissioners offered French mediation to Ali, pasha of Janina. The Ottoman periphery turns to France for arbitration.
tweets.nap-17980124-10: I received your letter announcing your Departure for Rome. Arrive as fast as you can. The march on Rome cannot wait.
tweets.nap-17980601-170: Soldiers, you sail to a conquest whose fruits for civilisation and commerce no man can measure. You will find the richest, most fertile land on earth. The English dogs who seized Egypt I will drive out; the Mameluke tyrants I will crush.
tweets.nap-17980601-27: I know of nothing more respectable and worthy of the veneration of men than a priest who, imbued with the true spirit of the Gospel, is persuaded that he is in duty bound to obey the temporal power, and to maintain peace, tranquillity, and union in his diocese.
tweets.nap-17980610-55: I eminence summoned aboard flagship over watering rights. The Bishop of Malta comes to the orient.
tweets.nap-17980610-56: I midnight: land two 12-pounders at saint-julien. The guns go ashore in darkness.
tweets.nap-17980701-171: Egyptians: You will be told by our enemies that I am come to destroy your religion. Believe them not. Tell them that I am come to restore your rights, punish your usurpers, and raise the true worship of Mahomet.
tweets.nap-17980702-54: I long enough have Egypt's beys insulted the French nation and heaped outrages on its merchants: their chastisement hour arrived. The French flag flies over Alexandria; the beys must answer for their crimes.
tweets.nap-17980703-58: I tomorrow noon: engineers-artillery council at headquarters. The technical arms confer on the campaign.
tweets.nap-17980703-59: I all consuls' houses currently held are needed for the forces. The diplomatic quarter becomes the military quarter.
tweets.nap-17980703-60: I every alexandrian armed within 24 hours of publication. The city mobilises for its defence.
tweets.nap-17980721-28: We have at Cairo, Citizen general, a very fine mint. We require all the ingots which we left at Alexandria, in exchange for the coin given to us by the merchants. I beg you will therefore assemble the merchants to whom the said ingots were given, and ask to have them back.
tweets.nap-17980901-29: A Portuguese squadron joined the English cruisers off Alexandria. I demand justice of you, Directors, for the Queen of Portugal's insolence. No ocean bars the road to Lisbon.
tweets.nap-17981001-81: I send you my Brother Louis with the standards taken from the Turks and Mamelukes. The customs of this country are not ours; it will require a long time for this people to become used to them. However, every day they know us better.
tweets.nap-17981202-31: Deriot marches twenty-five troopers by night to Sulkowski, gathers thirty of the twenty-second, and strikes Matarzeh before dawn. Return by the Nile and learn the ground for the next ambush. I demand exact hours.
tweets.nap-17981202-61: Secret meeting at your house: Perree, Dumanoir, Barre. The naval commanders confer in secrecy.
tweets.nap-17981203-62: I draft every convoy sailor under twenty-five, all nations. The fleet needs men.
tweets.nap-17981204-63: I spent the night at Birket el-Hâggy with a battalion and two guns.
tweets.nap-17981207-64: I have received the Coptic nation’s letter. The Copts have long been debased, and I place them under French protection.
tweets.nap-17981207-65: I survey gizych: villages and influential men. Intelligence maps the territory.
tweets.nap-17981207-66: I no free boats; artillery pays for boats. Every resource serves the army.
tweets.nap-17981221-30: Perverse men led some of you astray; they have perished. God has ordered me to be clement and merciful to the people; I have been clement and merciful towards you. I was angry with you for revolting. During two months I deprived you of your divan; but today I restore it.
tweets.nap-17990102-32: You have already been informed of my arrival on the shores of the Red sea, with a numerous and invincible army, animated with the desire of delivering you from the iron yoke of England.
tweets.nap-17990102-67: Your letter received and read with pleasure. The Divan's correspondence is acknowledged.
tweets.nap-17990105-68: I want foot guides and 100 men of the Ninth, with a double-hitched 3-pounder, marching at five tomorrow morning.
tweets.nap-17990107-69: Back from desert ride: your letters and measures approved. The reconnaissance confirms our plans.
tweets.nap-17990107-70: I want every possible effort made to collect the tax returns.
tweets.nap-17990108-71: I behead abou-chayr, divan member, convicted of treason. Justice is swift for traitors.
tweets.nap-17990110-72: I am forming dromedary units with ten men each from the Maltese and naval legions.
tweets.nap-17990110-73: Extremely displeased Menou kept the Revanche from Damietta. My orders were clear; disobedience will not be tolerated.
tweets.nap-17990125-185: Tippoo Sahib, you know of my coming to the Red Sea shores with a numerous, invincible army. Eager to free you from England's iron yoke, I ask you to send me by Muscat or Mocha word of your political state.
tweets.nap-17990205-74: I write citadel and forts for their returns. The garrison status must be reported.
tweets.nap-17990205-75: Six 6-inch mortars placed at your disposal. The siege train is ready.
tweets.nap-17990210-76: A Ragusan entered Alexandria with Hamelin and Livron aboard. Neutral ships bring our officers.
tweets.nap-17990214-77: I an engineer at once to the el-arich road wells. Water supply determines the march.
tweets.nap-17990214-78: Murat departs tomorrow at first light. I send my cavalry chief to his post.
tweets.nap-17990215-79: I march this morning, with the cavalry following.
tweets.nap-17990215-80: I pay chest, shoes and clothing all into Fort Qatyeh. The forward depot is stocked.
tweets.nap-17990301-33: The General-in-Chief Bonaparte commanding the armies of the French Republic begs me to inform you that in virtue of the cartel of exchange between the two nations, he sends you the English prisoners captured at Hayfa.
tweets.nap-17990304-81: I troops burning camp straw and wood on leaving: rarest objects. Waste is forbidden; every resource serves the army.
tweets.nap-17990307-82: I have come to Palestine to drive out tyrants, and I offer Abdallah peace.
tweets.nap-17990309-83: El-Arich fell after three days of open trench. I order the siege works pressed rapidly.
tweets.nap-17990309-84: I take 30-100 Egyptians at Jaffa for a company. Local recruits join the French colours.
tweets.nap-17990309-85: I sequester every magazine; gontier to Jaffa. All supplies are confiscated for the army.
tweets.nap-17990402-01: By your description, the castle clearly commands neither the Jordan crossing nor the Damascus road. The position is not as you reported; adjust your dispositions accordingly.
tweets.nap-17990402-02: I dispatch a vessel to Damietta with army news and General Dommartin's letters. The courier sails with dispatches.
tweets.nap-17990405-03: I will draw the men stationed at Haifa to strengthen Daoud’s mill post. Hold the position.
tweets.nap-17990405-04: I sent a boat with a naval officer to tell you our need of powder and shot. The supply line must not fail.
tweets.nap-17990409-05: The General-in-Chief orders all your light infantry to march at once for Nazareth. The vanguard moves now.
tweets.nap-17990410-06: I citizen larrey will send daily a health officer to serve in the trench. The wounded are cared for even under fire.
tweets.nap-17990413-07: Move before dawn with the fourth light demi-brigade. I expect the night march to begin on the hour.
tweets.nap-17990415-08: I will take a position between Nazareth and Soulyn village at once.
tweets.nap-17990418-09: I have defeated the Damascus janissaries and Djezzar’s cavalry at Nazareth after they crossed the Jordan to relieve Acre.
tweets.nap-17990419-10: I general baraguey d'hilliers will weigh from Genoa, weather permitting, on 6 or at latest 7 Floreal. The reinforcements sail on schedule.
tweets.nap-17990501-173: Soldiers: You have traversed the desert which separates Asia from Africa with the rapidity of an Arab force. The army which was on its march to invade Egypt is destroyed. You have taken its general, its field-artillery, camels, and baggage.
tweets.nap-17990504-86: My scouts hold tonight right sap; the siege works continue through the night.
tweets.nap-17990509-87: I judge the breach has made the Great Tower untenable under fire from the Pharos.
tweets.nap-17990509-88: I midnight: occupy the second tower crest. The assault continues in darkness.
tweets.nap-17990513-89: I order the twenty-second light to Hayfa with dromedaries. The camel column moves at once.
tweets.nap-17990516-90: I move 400 wounded to tantourah tomorrow morning. The evacuation of casualties begins at dawn.
tweets.nap-17990516-91: I move wounded to Jaffa or the frigates. Casualties go to the nearest care.
tweets.nap-17990517-92: Soldiers, you crossed the Africa-Asia desert faster than an Arab army. The feat of arms is unprecedented.
tweets.nap-17990602-11: I general robin marches today at noon for mesoudyah, resting long enough for soup, water and rest. The column moves with proper pauses.
tweets.nap-17990602-12: Leave at Qatyeh all Christians sheltered with us from Acre or Jaffa. The protected civilians remain in safety.
tweets.nap-17990602-13: I have stationed the first battalion of the Third at Fort El-Arich until further orders.
tweets.nap-17990615-14: I thank General Dugua for his conduct during my absence in Syria.
tweets.nap-17990615-15: I arrived yesterday with part of the army. I left a good garrison in Fort El-Arich. The return to Egypt is complete.
tweets.nap-17990617-16: I am sending General Desaix to Rahyreh province; the naval legion will leave Rosetta.
tweets.nap-17990619-17: I learned with pleasure your occupation of Qoseyr. Engineers are ordered to you. The Red sea port is secured.
tweets.nap-17990621-18: Yesterday I inspected Cairo citadel myself; Citizen Fauvi takes an improper tone with the commandant. I correct the insubordination personally.
tweets.nap-17990622-19: I inspected the citadel works and commend Brigade Chief Dupas’s extraordinary activity.
tweets.nap-17990623-20: Hassan-Toubar leaves me. Tonight he hands over his son as hostage, a man of thirty. The tribal alliance is secured by the hostage.
tweets.nap-17990701-34: There is no God but God, and Mohammed is his prophet. To the Divan of Cairo, wisest and most enlightened: I pray the Prophet's grace be on you. Eighty vessels showed before Alexandria; warmly met, they anchor at Aboukir landing troops.
tweets.nap-17990702-93: Your Messidor letter is here, with Friant's. I note both. Correspondence with my generals is current.
tweets.nap-17990703-94: Your El-Senytali letter received; all cavalry in Bahyreh. The horse is concentrated where needed.
tweets.nap-17990704-95: I have ended the customs farm at Qoseyr; the Suez customs rules now apply there.
tweets.nap-17990705-96: I friant: Mourad still at hayan fountain. Drive him out. The rebel chief must be pursued.
tweets.nap-17990707-97: Your report is here; Mourad never left the Rayan springs. I see the foe sits fast. Hold him under your eye.
tweets.nap-17990709-98: Both your letters are here. I read them with attention. The intelligence is noted; carry on.
tweets.nap-17990709-99: Your two Talia letters are here; we must concentrate. I order the forces gathered for the next blow.
tweets.nap-17990801-174: Europe's news sends me to France. I leave Kleber my army. You shall hear from me soon. It rends me to quit troops I love. Italy is lost; Mantua, Turin, Tortona invested. Starved of succour and scourged by plague, you may treat with Turkey, even to quitting Egypt.
tweets.nap-17990801-35: I have not been well satisfied with your operations during the movements which have just taken place. No matter what events arise, nothing should hinder a soldier from obeying orders; talent in war consists in overcoming obstacles, not causing failure.
tweets.nap-17990802-100: I have taken Aboukir fort, the enemy’s battle reserve.
tweets.nap-17990804-101: Aboukir summoned; the pasha's son will yield. I grant the capitulation.
tweets.nap-17990811-102: Little satisfied with all your operations in this movement. Desaix, your performance disappoints me.
tweets.nap-17990811-103: On Syria return you would pass 150,000 livres to the paymaster. The financial obligation stands.
tweets.nap-17990811-104: I extremely displeased with zajonchek's negligent execution. The subordinate failed his duty.
tweets.nap-17990811-105: Your 18 Thermidor received; projects fully approved. Desaix, this time your plans have my full backing.
tweets.nap-17990812-106: Keep my guides and crews. Lannes, the essential personnel stay with the command.
tweets.nap-17990822-36: You will find inclosed, Citizen general, an order to take over the command in chief of the army. The fear of English cruisers returning makes me hasten my departure. I take with me Berthier, Lannes, Murat, Andreossy, and Marmont, the citizens Monge and Berthollet.
tweets.nap-17990822-81: I take with me Berthier, Lannes, Murat, Andreossy, and Marmont, the citizens Monge and Berthollet. The core staff departs with me for France.
tweets.nap-17991010-37: Citizen Directors, since I left France I have received only one of your despatches, which reached me when I was before Acre. It contained the news of our successes at Naples, which made me conjecture an approaching war on the Continent.
tweets.nap-17991101-175: Army of the East: France acknowledged all the influence of your conquests on the restoration of her trade and civilization of the world. The eyes of all Europe are upon you, and in thought I am often with you. The Republic honours your service in the East.
tweets.nap-18000102-21: I have sent the draft rules for reorganizing the Paris National Guard to the Interior section.
tweets.nap-18000104-22: I whereas Brigade chief dupuy, dead arms in hand at Cairo, commanded the through five campaigns. The fallen hero is honoured.
tweets.nap-18000104-23: I am satisfied with your conduct in the division. Enlighten the people; Let all citizens feel that parties and strife are past. The division commander earns my confidence.
tweets.nap-18000105-24: Tell me Pichegru's conduct abroad since 18 Fructidor Year V. Truth is wanted, not calumny. The Consul demands facts, not slander.
tweets.nap-18000105-25: You asked 15,000 men. Consul Bonaparte charges me to answer by extraordinary courier. The First Consul directs the war effort.
tweets.nap-18000108-26: Chouan bands gather in Orne. The First Consul complains of hearing nothing from you. The rebellion in the west demands attention.
tweets.nap-18000108-27: I want the War Minister to report immediately on the state of the clothing administration.
tweets.nap-18000109-28: I saw with indignation that Chouans have settled at Saint-Jean-de-Margon.
tweets.nap-18000109-29: I have ordered General Gardanne and the England Army officers to be ready to embark before the month ends.
tweets.nap-18000501-38: I have just received your letter of the Floreal.
tweets.nap-18000601-176: Soldiers: When we began our march, one department of France was in the hands of the enemy. Consternation pervaded the south of the Republic. You advanced. Joy and hope in our country have succeeded to consternation and fear.
tweets.nap-18000601-178: Sire, amid my wounded and fifteen thousand corpses I beg you hear humanity: let not two brave nations cut throats for others' interests. I write from the field itself.
tweets.nap-18000620-39: Write to General Kleber that when the news of the capitulation arrived, the Brest squadron was about to sail with 4,000 troops and war stores; we have only just learned the capitulation has been broken, and he has reconquered Egypt.
tweets.nap-18000620-81: I write to General Kleber: when capitulation news arrived, the Brest squadron was about to sail with 4,000 troops and war stores; the capitulation was broken, and he has reconquered Egypt.
tweets.nap-18000621-40: I ask you to invite two leading singers to Paris for an Italian duet at the national fête. Provide for their travel; I have chosen Madame Billington and Madame Grassini.
tweets.nap-18000922-81: I refused ratification of the peace preliminaries after intrigues by the faction opposed to peace.
tweets.nap-18010102-01: I legislators, the Republic triumphs. Hohenlinden's victory resounded through Europe. The French arms have prevailed.
tweets.nap-18010104-02: I have ordered the Navy Minister to arrest Citizen Tallien, who is accused of leaving Egypt without a passport.
tweets.nap-18010107-03: I hand m. De muzquiz a letter complaining of changed preparations against Portugal. The diplomatic pressure on Lisbon continues.
tweets.nap-18010107-04: I have told General Menou that Aboukir is the only place for a serious landing in Egypt.
tweets.nap-18010109-05: I thank you for your news of the extraordinary 3 Nivose event. The Consul acknowledges the report.
tweets.nap-18010109-06: I forty men leave bicetre tomorrow for orleans, thence to embark at Nantes. The conscripts move to the embarkation port.
tweets.nap-18010113-07: Brune putting Tuscany under your orders seems to me extremely wise. The command structure in Italy is rationalised.
tweets.nap-18010114-08: I a law will Let Ajaccio sell lands to bring water. The birthplace of the Consul gets its aqueduct.
tweets.nap-18010114-09: I combis's mission: remind santo domingo's people the land is now French. The colony remembers its allegiance.
tweets.nap-18010114-10: I general toussaint louverture, amid revolutionary storms, saved France a great colony by prudence and courage. The black general earns the consul's respect.
tweets.nap-18010119-11: I draft a treaty for helvetia to cede all Valais to brigg. The Swiss cantons yield territory to France.
tweets.nap-18010121-12: I yesterday a Russian courier arrived in fifteen days with an extremely friendly letter. The czar's overture is welcome.
tweets.nap-18010204-13: I dispatch a night courier to General Murat, reaching foligno tomorrow. The urgent orders ride through the night.
tweets.nap-18010302-14: Send Madrid the great interest I take in Spain's navy acting again. The Spanish fleet must return to the seas.
tweets.nap-18010302-15: I am sending Brigade Chief Savary to Lorient without delay.
tweets.nap-18010402-16: We Consuls have found major discrepancies in the military accountants’ ledgers. I want them reconciled.
tweets.nap-18010503-17: I several of georges's band wish to submit. The chouan rebels seek amnesty.
tweets.nap-18010504-18: I have ordered the War Minister to gather battalions at Brest.
tweets.nap-18010601-35: I see with pleasure that you are ready to sail. Your arrival in the Mediterranean is all the more important because the English are preparing to reinforce their army at Aboukir. The fleet must contest the Eastern Mediterranean.
tweets.nap-18010602-19: I notify by express that moncey commands French troops in Cisalpine. The command appointment is announced at speed.
tweets.nap-18010702-20: I tell him: 'doge' and 'podestat' suit liguria better. The ligurian constitution reflects its own traditions.
tweets.nap-18010704-21: I have sent the frigates Bravoure, Carrère, and Succès to Livorno to cruise.
tweets.nap-18010806-22: I tell journalists, political and literary, to abstain from all religious matter. The Press must not inflame theological disputes.
tweets.nap-18010806-23: I send levavasseur post to Brest to inspect coast batteries. The coastal defences are inspected.
tweets.nap-18010905-24: I have ordered the Year X army organization updated without changing soldiers’ pay.
tweets.nap-18010905-25: I read the committee's observations; nothing reasonable in them. The Consul dismisses the committee's critique.
tweets.nap-18011003-26: I have the salines' receipts. Warn the farmers the government watches. The salt monopoly is enforced.
tweets.nap-18011004-27: I have ordered Theophilanthrope societies to stop meeting in national buildings.
tweets.nap-18011006-28: I have a handy medium saber modelled. The cavalry weapon is standardised.
tweets.nap-18011108-29: I saint-domingue's people, whatever origin or color, are all Frenchmen, all free, all equal before God and Republic. Liberty, equality, fraternity for all.
tweets.nap-18011109-30: Frenchmen, yours at last entire, this peace earned by such long generous efforts! The Amiens peace is won by your sacrifices.
tweets.nap-18011202-31: I tell montchoisy Paris disowns the Helvetic government. The Swiss puppet regime has no French backing.
tweets.nap-18011204-32: I citizen sage reports volta's hard case at Paris. The scientist's situation is reviewed.
tweets.nap-18020202-30: I am sending Citizen Lebrun to Turin tonight with the enclosed letter for General Jourdan.
tweets.nap-18020202-31: I hasten to Tell Your Holiness the Cisalpine Republic's affairs are arranged. The Italian Sister Republic is settled.
tweets.nap-18020202-32: General Silly reports Your Majesty's welcome to 300 French forced by sea onto Sicily. The Neapolitan king shows hospitality to our castaways.
tweets.nap-18020202-33: Your 12 Pluviose letter received. All moves at Amiens. Eight days more or less are now indifferent. The peace negotiations proceed at their own pace.
tweets.nap-18020205-34: I am considering the minister’s proposal to confirm Fournier’s promotion despite his shortfall in seniority.
tweets.nap-18020206-35: I have ordered the memoirs, plans, and scientific findings from the Egypt expedition published at government expense.
tweets.nap-18020207-36: I am sending Citizen Lauriston to Brest to await the departure of Bouvet’s squadron.
tweets.nap-18020210-37: Glad to read you firmly constituted. You are a small state; live tranquil; shun faction. Lucca's independence depends on unity.
tweets.nap-18020607-81: A Barbary ship has been blockading a dozen Ligurian vessels at St. Tropez, and the Maritime Prefect has done nothing to disengage the port. It is a dishonour to the Republic that these Barbary wretches should insult our Coasts.
tweets.nap-18020906-81: I send you a note forwarded by the Inspector general of Gendarmery concerning the Bishop of Rennes.
tweets.nap-18021202-38: I propose that six bishops remain in Piedmont, using France’s one-bishop-per-two-departments rule as a guide.
tweets.nap-18021202-39: I report on wood-cutting bills as paper money. The forest revenue is audited.
tweets.nap-18021202-40: I direct only Germinal and Messidor timber receipts to fund Year XI; the rest to Year XII.
tweets.nap-18021202-41: I want General Brune to demand the immediate return of Citizen Ruffin’s ship, seized by Djezzar-Pasha.
tweets.nap-18021204-42: I have given Beauvoisin all his copies of the Ambigu and the Ivernois pamphlet.
tweets.nap-18021207-43: I order Ré, Oléron and Sainte-Marguerite to hold all sentenced deportees. The island prisons receive the condemned.
tweets.nap-18021210-44: Deputies, your fatherland is critical. Moderation, prudence, sacrificed passions alone can save it. Switzerland's survival depends on restraint.
tweets.nap-18021210-45: I order plans for Quiberon, belle-ile and Boulogne batteries. The coastal defences are planned.
tweets.nap-18030203-46: Read the enclosed report. 'Liquidation of newly created pensions' means nothing to me. The pension accounts are opaque.
tweets.nap-18030203-47: I have coordinated the convoys from Havre, Dunkerque, Toulon, Genoa, and Corsica so their troops arrive together.
tweets.nap-18030204-48: Glad of Fort Dauphin retaken; take directly my full confidence and approval of vigorous measures. Rochambeau earns my trust.
tweets.nap-18030205-49: I fifteen thousand men shipped or shipping to saint-domingue. Combine now a 6,500 expedition. The colony receives massive reinforcements.
tweets.nap-18030208-50: I order the brisgau commander to receive two Austrian companies. The border garrison accepts the enemy detachment.
tweets.nap-18030208-51: My trust in your great talents bids me ask an elementary mathematics work for the national lycees. Haüy, write the textbook for the new schools.
tweets.nap-18030209-52: I have received Telemague’s letter thanking me for his appointment as mayor of Cap and affirming his loyalty to the Republic.
tweets.nap-18030210-53: Madame de Staël, barred from Paris, has reached Melun. I have ordered the police to send her straight back.
tweets.nap-18030501-01: Your letter reached me at the Malmaison. I desire that the conference should not degenerate into a conversation. Show yourself cold, haughty, and even somewhat proud.
tweets.nap-18030623-24: I have received your letter, good little Josephine. I perceived with sorrow that you suffered from the journey. But a few days of repose will do much for you. I am very well.
tweets.nap-18030701-25: I have received your letter of the of. You do not speak of your health, or of the effect of the baths. I see that you intend to be on your return in eight days. That will afford great pleasure to your Friend, who wearies of being alone.
tweets.nap-18030801-02: Irish affairs move me to order secret talks with the United Irish chiefs in Paris. Offer them twenty-five thousand men, forty thousand muskets, guns and powder, and pledge no peace with England till Ireland stands free, if twenty thousand join us on landing.
tweets.nap-18030901-03: I return you the despatch from Madrid of the Fructidor. I am surprised that we have no other news. Make out a list of all the complaints we have against Spain, so that we may have materials ready in the event of requiring them.
tweets.nap-18031110-04: I return you your despatches, Citizen minister. Tell Citizen Laforest that I have read his despatch with great interest. It will be well to warn the Turkish ambassador that the English, who evidently encourage the Beys, intend to seize upon Egypt.
tweets.nap-18031112-05: Citizen general, I have received your letter, and have given orders for hoods to be served out to all the men forming part of the expedition to Ireland, of which you shall have the command. Affairs are settled with Spain and Portugal. Measures have been taken against desertion.
tweets.nap-18040101-34: My Friend, I have not received any news from you for several days; I should, however, have been glad to know what effect the waters have had, and how you pass your time. I have been here for the last week, and intend going tomorrow to Boulogne.
tweets.nap-18040214-06: For the last week we have been in pursuit of forty brigands composed of Georges and his band, who disembarked at three different places. Another band is to disembark; we have arrested all the men who were to make signals. Savary awaits them at Biville.
tweets.nap-18040301-81: You have no doubt heard that Pichegru was arrested yesterday. He was unable to make use of his pistols or of his sabre. He fought with his fists for half an hour with three or four gendarmes. The pleasure experienced by the people of Paris at this arrest does them credit.
tweets.nap-18040310-07: I ordered the Duke d’Enghien taken secretly to Vincennes under the name Plessis.
tweets.nap-18040410-08: I thank your Holiness for having given a cardinal's hat to the Archbishop of Bologna. I have come to the determination to take into my own hands all that relates to the Concordat with the Italian Republic.
tweets.nap-18040510-09: Steube, the minister of Wirtemberg, is a downright fool, as ill-meaning as ignorant. If you can insinuate in a delicate manner that he ought to be recalled, that would please me. Write to General Lannes at Lisbon, and mention the matter to M.
tweets.nap-18040530-10: Send Hawkesbury's note to all my agents save Russia, Sweden, Denmark, Porte, with my gloss: gross as its insults run, contempt were my due reply, but England's open maxims overturn Europe's order and must be answered.
tweets.nap-18040610-11: This wretched Moreau trial keeps me from the camps. I hope it ends within days. Camp and Paris buzz of a continental war; that would be fatal, turning us from England. Woe to war-seekers! Germany, Austria, Prussia stand with us.
tweets.nap-18040712-12: I desire that you will give me by return of post some information on the subject of the family of the Elector of Bavaria, especially concerning His Daughter, and his intentions with regard to that young princess.
tweets.nap-18040721-13: Madam and dear Wife, for the last four days since I have been absent from you I have been constantly on horseback, and this exercise has not impaired my health. M. Maret tells me that you intend starting on Monday.
tweets.nap-18040803-201: My love, I hope to hear shortly that the waters have done you very much good. I am pained that you have met with so many annoyances. I desire that you should write me often. My health is very good, although I am a little fatigued.
tweets.nap-18040806-02: My love, I have been at Calais since midnight. I think of setting out this evening for Dunkirk. I am satisfied with what I see, and am in very good health. I hope that the waters may benefit you, as much as the bustle, the sight of camps, and the ocean have me.
tweets.nap-18040901-14: I d'oubril has gone. Although this departure is not good news, still it does not mean a rupture; but it is incalculable what may happen within two or three months. And on the same day Fouche was ordered not to allow any Russians to leave Paris without having paid their debts.
tweets.nap-18040910-15: Holy Father, restored faith has remade my people's morals. Crown my work: come anoint the first French Emperor yourself. Your hands lend heaven's light; our peoples draw the Almighty's blessing on our decrees.
tweets.nap-18040914-16: Everywhere my police farmers coin money from gaming tables. I mean the towns to profit instead; Bordeaux tables yield two hundred thousand francs for a bridge or canal. To Berthier: Ireland is decided.
tweets.nap-18040916-17: Sir, my Uncle and Cousin, General Cafferelli is the bearer of the enclosed letter for the Pope. The Holy father will travel in his own carriages to the foot of Mont Cenis; arrived there, my carriages will bring him on.
tweets.nap-18041001-18: My friend, I reach Treves as you reach St Cloud. Grant T no audience. See B only in public, never alone. Sign no marriage contract till I have signed. To Fouche: Boulogne prefecture burned days before the English tried our flotilla.
tweets.nap-18041006-202: My love, I have arrived at Treves. At the same hour you reach St. Cloud. I am well. Do not grant an audience to T. Refuse to see him. Do not receive B. except publicly. Do not give him a private audience.
tweets.nap-18041029-19: You will see in the Moniteur of tomorrow an account of an unheard-of attack by the English on four Spanish frigates. Have several articles inserted in the papers with the object of exciting France to war, and of indisposing as much as possible the other powers against England.
tweets.nap-18041110-20: Sir, my Brother, I received your Majesty's letter this evening, and was much touched by the expressions of confidence and friendship which it contained. My first movement after reading your letter was to give orders for the immediate release of M. Rumbold.
tweets.nap-18041203-179: Behold your colors! These eagles will always be your rallying point! They will always be where your Emperor may think them necessary for the defence of his throne and of his people.
tweets.nap-18041210-21: I write you this letter to make known my displeasure in that you have permitted the word 'supper' to be used in the invitations of Wednesday, since the hour for which they are issued is that of my dinner.
tweets.nap-18050102-180: My Brother: Called to the throne by Providence, by the suffrages of the Senate, of the people, and of the army, my first desire is peace. France and England, abusing their prosperity, may contend for ages. But I desire peace, and I hope that England will not refuse it.
tweets.nap-18050130-22: Most high, most excellent, most powerful, most magnanimous and invincible prince, great Emperor of the Mussulmans, Sultan Selim, in whom honour and virtue abound, our very dear and perfect friend, may God augment your grandeur and accord you a happy end.
tweets.nap-18050201-23: The present letter will be presented to your royal highness by General Junot, my ambassador.
tweets.nap-18050310-24: Many people complain that classical books cost too much. I want a commission to set a per-page price for books used in the lycées.
tweets.nap-18050401-25: Your courier tells me Dominica fell. My Toulon squadron sailed a fortnight ago with Lauriston's division; no news yet. England bleeds in India; Decaen arms the Mahrattas with guns and officers. A Walcheren venture is madness.
tweets.nap-18050410-26: I beg you will inform M. De Moustier that I cannot conceive how a man of so much judgment allows 30,000 Russians to alarm him for Prussia which has 300,000 men. The artillery, cavalry, and officers of the Prussian army are worth thirty times those of Russia.
tweets.nap-18050421-27: I forward you a report concerning Creusot. It is essential to keep up this establishment. It will not be well to purchase it; but I think it will be useful to give a fixed amount of orders, so that it may have a basis of operations, and be able to support itself. To M.
tweets.nap-18050506-181: Jerome fancies some weakness in me will indulge him. Having no father's rights, I bear no father's blind love; a father loves being blind, seeing himself in his son. I cannot be blinded where duty rules. Let him earn, not presume.
tweets.nap-18050506-28: Sir, my Brother-in-law and Cousin, what you write concerning the conclusion of a treaty of alliance between England and Russia is nonsense; it is entirely false. These reports, spread by the English so that they may for the moment escape from their difficulties, are unfounded.
tweets.nap-18050526-29: I want letters printed as from Petersburg: Frenchmen well used there, court and town for friendship, English greed blamed for the war, their coalition broken, Russia still.
tweets.nap-18050529-30: The people of Genoa appear to desire their union to France. The advantages of this union, and circumstances, are such as to induce me to pay no attention to the blustering of a few powers. In fact, this can excite the animadversion of England alone.
tweets.nap-18050601-31: As nothing would give me a better idea of the exact feeling of the court of Vienna than a negotiation with the view of exchanging a certain number of cordons of the legion of honour against Austrian cordons, write to M. de la Rochefoucauld to tell M.
tweets.nap-18050720-32: I think I ordered you to embark everything, for circumstances may present themselves at any moment. I wish you to embark the artillery, powder, and all the ammunitions, so that in twenty-four hours the whole expedition may start.
tweets.nap-18050727-33: I have directed M. Marescalchi to forward you a decree, ordering the Legislative body to terminate its sittings. My intention is that during my reign in Italy it shall not meet again. I had too good an opinion of the Italians.
tweets.nap-18050731-34: All the news I receive from Italy is warlike, and Austria no longer conceals her intentions. Prepare a note for M. de Cobentzel, let it be long, wily, argumentative, and in similar terms to the inclosed. The note drawn up by Talleyrand was approved of, and forwarded to Vienna.
tweets.nap-18050814-38: With thirty sail my admirals should not fear twenty-four English, or disband the navy. If Villeneuve idles at Ferrol past my deadline I call him the basest of men. London says Nelson roams far.
tweets.nap-18050901-182: Soldiers, the third coalition's war is opened. Austria crossed the Inn, broke treaties, drove our ally from his capital. You yourselves were forced to double-march to our frontiers. They forced this war on us; answer with the courage that ever marks French arms.
tweets.nap-18050901-39: I have arrived at Strasburg. All the army has passed the Rhine. The enemy is at the issues of the Black Forest. Our manoeuvres will soon commence. Do all you can to induce the nation to adopt the conscription.
tweets.nap-18051002-40: My brother, yours received. Prussia never cared about troops crossing Baireuth and Anspach; we crossed that country at will all last war. A month ago I promised to stand mid-Germany by early next month; with God's help I soon restore you to Munich.
tweets.nap-18051002-41: My good Josephine, I have fatigued myself more than was prudent. All day long for a whole week wet to the skin, and the feet cold, have made me rather unwell; but I have not been out to-day, and that has reposed me.
tweets.nap-18051023-203: The two last nights have rested me much, and I shall leave tomorrow for Munich. I send for M. de Talleyrand and M. de Maret to be near me. I shall see them but little. Talleyrand was then minister of Foreign affairs.
tweets.nap-18051101-43: I think there will be no inconvenience in your coming to meet me at the Abbaye de Moelk. You can pass by Braunau where you will see General Lauriston. The Emperor of Germany is still at Vienna. He has written me several letters, and would like to come to an arrangement.
tweets.nap-18051102-42: Sire, I send Savary, my aide, to greet your arrival. I charge him to avow my esteem and my hunger for chances to prove how I covet your friendship. Receive him with your famed kindness, and count me foremost among those who would please you.
tweets.nap-18051116-204: I write to M. D'Harville in order that you set out, and that you proceed to Baden, from thence to Stuttgard, and from there to Munich. You will give at Stuttgard the wedding present to the Princess Paul. It is sufficient that it cost fifteen to twenty thousand francs.
tweets.nap-18051202-44: My brother, yours received. Talks drag on; my army rests. Charles's host lies close. Likely, if peace lags, within weeks comes a stroke leaving Austria not a shadow of resource. I wait, ready.
tweets.nap-18051202-45: I have received your letter of the Nivose. The Emperor and Prince Charles have written to me. I shall have an interview with the archduke at three leagues from Vienna. I send you a copy of my letter to the Emperor, who has written to me in the most amiable manner.
tweets.nap-18051203-184: I am satisfied with you. In the battle of Austerlitz you have justified all that I expected from your intrepidity. You have decorated your eagles with immortal glory.
tweets.nap-18051203-205: I have dispatched Lebrun to you from the field of battle. I have beaten the Austrian and Russian armies commanded by the two Emperors. I am a little fatigued. I have bivouacked eight days in the open air, through some very cold nights.
tweets.nap-18051203-46: After manoeuvring for a few days I fought a decisive battle yesterday. I defeated the combined armies commanded by the Emperors of Russia and of Germany. Their force consisted of 80,000 Russians and 30,000 Austrians.
tweets.nap-18051205-206: I have concluded a truce. The Russians have gone home again. The battle of Austerlitz is the most glorious of all which I have gained.
tweets.nap-18051207-207: I have concluded an armistice. Before eight days, peace will be made. I hope to learn that you have arrived at Munich, in good health. The Russians have retired. They have sustained an immense loss; more than twenty thousand killed and thirty thousand taken.
tweets.nap-18051214-50: The Emperor of Germany asked for an interview, which I granted; it lasted from 2 till 4 P.M. I will tell you what I think of him when I see you. He wished to conclude peace on the spot.
tweets.nap-18051225-49: My Brother, I send you a letter for the minister of the treasury (M. Barbe-Marbois). You will read it, then seal it and hand it to him. I do not yet know whether it is incapacity or treason, but the coalition has had no more useful ally than this minister.
tweets.nap-18060112-52: You will stand near Rome within days. I send Dumas; Massena should be there. After brief rest count forty thousand in three corps: Massena strongest, St Cyr another, Regnier a six-thousand reserve. Befriend cold Regnier; he plans best.
tweets.nap-18060124-53: Occupy Frankfort with one division, levying nothing yet. Only with your whole corps united will you demand four millions for the Grand Army's chest. I decree victory beforehand, after the Convention's fashion.
tweets.nap-18060410-54: My Cousin, the affairs of Cattaro are not getting settled; however, I have decided to remain in Germany until I know how matters are likely to turn out. Keep an eye on the movements of the Austrians.
tweets.nap-18060422-55: My Brother, I see with pleasure that you have burned an insurgent village. I suppose that you allowed the soldiers to pillage it. That is the way in which villages which revolt should be treated. It is the right of war, and it is also a duty prescribed by policy.
tweets.nap-18060501-58: My sister, yours received. Exact no oaths from priests; it breeds trouble. Go your way; shut the convents. I published the Concordat at Lucca and the Pope meddled; my sharp note answered. What saves souls at Bologna saves at Lucca. Ask Pius if he takes me for a weak prince.
tweets.nap-18060510-56: After all the difficulties in the way of constructing the Arc de Triomphe on the site of the Bastille, I consent to its being constructed at the gate of Chaillot, at l'Etoile [where it now stands].
tweets.nap-18060510-57: My son, Lemarois should be at Ancona by now; I give him my Papal States troops. He is an old trusted aide, witness of my midnight civil wedding to Josephine before a sleepy mayor. I trust him fully.
tweets.nap-18060510-59: I am not at all surprised that you are satisfied with Marshal Jourdan. I was equally satisfied with him in the administration of Italy; he is an upright, active, and methodical man. I do not see why you leave Massena at Capua.
tweets.nap-18060513-60: I see with pleasure the energy which you display in governing. The forty-four individuals condemned to death and to the galleys is a salutary measure, which will serve as an example, and will check those who desire to indulge in their natural inconstancy.
tweets.nap-18060516-61: My Cousin, I have re-called you from Rome because it is not in accordance with my dignity that you should remain at so ill-conducted a court which does all it can to annoy me, and which I shall be constrained to punish sooner or later.
tweets.nap-18060610-62: I asked you for a note on the forces of Prussia. The information contained in the letters of Laforest is not what I want. I require to know the general situation of the army of the king of Prussia.
tweets.nap-18060610-63: Lord Yarmouth has arrived, with full powers from the king of England to sign peace. We should be tolerably well agreed but for Sicily. The English will recognise you as king of Naples, but, as you have not taken Sicily, they cannot recognise you there.
tweets.nap-18060610-64: I see with pleasure that you are satisfied with the Dutch. The pretensions of your finance minister are out of the question. My expenses are heavy, and I cannot aid you as I should like. As long as the war lasts I shall be obliged to keep up my army.
tweets.nap-18060619-65: Inform M. Alquier that I regard the Pope from a temporal and from a spiritual point of view. As a temporal prince he forms part of my confederation, whether he likes it or no.
tweets.nap-18060702-66: We have no news from General Regnier. The art of war about which every one speaks is a difficult art; you have not a man in your council who understands the first notions of it. I have concluded peace with Russia (treaty not ratified). Negotiations are going on with England.
tweets.nap-18060726-67: It is my intention to organise nine metropolitan seminaries without delay. Present me a report on the number of priests necessary.
tweets.nap-18060807-69: I send you a letter, which will make you thoroughly acquainted with that scamp Lucchesini. My opinion was formed long ago with respect to that wretch. He has continually deceived you, because I have long perceived that nothing is more easy.
tweets.nap-18060810-70: My Son, I send you a copy of the catechism, which has been adopted for France; it would be a good thing if it could be adopted for Italy without inconvenience. But it is a delicate matter, and you must be very circumspect. Consult the minister of worship.
tweets.nap-18060814-68: My Son, I thank you for what you say about my fete day. Affairs are getting settled. I will soon send you instructions for your voyage to Paris. I know that you wish to come here. You will see the queen of Holland. We will keep the princess until after her confinement.
tweets.nap-18060830-71: My daughter, yours pleased me. Trust my love. Guard yourself in your state, and give us no daughter, if you please! I could give a recipe, did you believe: a glass of pure wine daily.
tweets.nap-18060907-73: I see with surprise that the chief of the staff dares to correspond with the enemy without your permission. General Caesar Berthier is then ignorant of his duty! The reply of Sidney Smith is impertinent, as is everything which emanates from that officer.
tweets.nap-18061001-77: I have received your letter. I was moved by Madame de Hatzfeld’s position. I convinced her that her husband was guilty and, under the laws of war, should be executed; I spared him even the ordeal of a trial.
tweets.nap-18061014-75: Immediately after the battle of Jena the king of Prussia sent me an aide-de-camp with a letter. Today he sends me the Marquis de Lucchesini. I have ordered him to remain at the outposts, and I have sent Duroc to know what he wants.
tweets.nap-18061015-188: Captive officers after Jena: I know not why I war with your sovereign, a wise, peaceable prince I respect. I would free your country from degrading vassalage to Prussia. Lay down ancient hatreds; France offers friendship.
tweets.nap-18061015-76: My Friend, I have manoeuvred finely against the Prussians. Yesterday I gained a great victory. They had 150,000 men. I took 30,000 prisoners, 100 guns and standards. I was in presence and close to the king of Prussia; I nearly captured him and the queen.
tweets.nap-18061023-208: I have received many letters from you. I can write you but a word. My Affairs are very prosperous. I shall be tomorrow at Potsdam, and the at Berlin. I am remarkably well; fatigue refreshes me.
tweets.nap-18061025-78: I have crushed the Prussian monarchy; I shall crush the Russians if they arrive. I no longer fear the Austrians. I shall not ask you for any troops; I have no need of them. If, however, you could send me some cavalry, do so.
tweets.nap-18061102-209: I have received your letter of the of. We have here superb weather. You will see by the bulletin that we have taken Stettin. It is a very strong place.
tweets.nap-18061121-79: I am at Kustrin in order to make some reconnaissances. I shall see, in two days, if you can come. Hold yourself in readiness. I hope that the queen of Holland will be of the party. It is two o'clock in the morning. I have just risen; this is the custom of war.
tweets.nap-18061127-80: I am going to take a town in Poland. This is the first town. This evening I shall be at Posen. After that I will call you to Berlin, so that we may arrive there on the same day. My health is good. The weather is rather bad; it has been raining for three days.
tweets.nap-18061201-81: I have a circular written, and take measures so that, throughout the extent of the empire, all letters coming from England, or written in English and by Englishmen, be seized. This is most important, as it is absolutely necessary to isolate England.
tweets.nap-18061201-82: Prussia, which had formed a league with Russia, has disappeared. I have destroyed her armies, and am master of her strong places. My armies are upon the Vistula, and Warsaw is in my power.
tweets.nap-18061202-210: Today is the anniversary of Austerlitz. I have been to a ball given by the city. It rains. I am well. I love you, and long for you. My troops are at Warsaw. It is not yet cold. All the Polish ladies are French, but there is only one woman for me.
tweets.nap-18061214-83: My Friend, I am starting for Warsaw. I shall be back in a fortnight, when I hope I shall be able to send for you. However, I should see you return to Paris, where you are desired, with pleasure. You know that I depend upon events. All my affairs are going on well.
tweets.nap-18061215-211: My love, I leave immediately for Warsaw. In a fortnight I shall be on my return. I hope that then I shall be able to send for you. Nevertheless, should there be still delay, I should see you with pleasure return to Paris, where you are desired.
tweets.nap-18061220-212: I have received no news from you, my love. I am very well. I have been at Warsaw for two days. My Affairs go on well. The weather is very mild, and even a little humid. We have as yet had scarcely any frost. It is the weather of. Adieu, my love.
tweets.nap-18061229-213: I can write you but a word, my love. I am in a wretched barn. I have beaten the Russians. I have taken thirty pieces of cannon, their baggage, and have made six thousand prisoners. But the weather is frightful. It rains; we have mud to the knees.
tweets.nap-18061231-84: I laughed heartily on receiving your last letter. You have formed an idea of the belles of Poland which they do not deserve. I received your letter in a wretched barn, having mud, wind, and straw for my bed. Tomorrow I shall be at Warsaw.
tweets.nap-18070102-85: I think that you have done wrong to create marshals, which has the inconvenience of costing money, and of giving men who have done little great pretensions. Do you think that a French general of Division would be commanded by a Dutch marshal?
tweets.nap-18070107-03: My love, I am deeply affected by all that you say to me; but the season cold, the roads wretched, the region unsafe, I cannot consent to expose you to such perils and dangers. Return to Paris, to pass the winter there.
tweets.nap-18070107-88: I have received your letter and thank you for your kind words. I value your attachment. What are you doing in Paris? I did not know you held a ball during Carnival.
tweets.nap-18070114-87: Turkey declared against Russia. A Tartar from Constantinople brings me prime news. A million comes to you from Turin. My health never stood better, whence, they tell me, I grow more gallant.
tweets.nap-18070114-91: I have received your letter. The affair in Hesse-Cassel is settled; it seems the soldiers wanted to move.
tweets.nap-18070116-86: My good friend, I have received your letter, and your grief pains me. Why these tears? I will see you soon. Do not doubt my affection; show greater strength of mind.
tweets.nap-18070118-214: I fear that you are greatly disappointed in view of our separation, which must yet be prolonged some weeks, and of your return to Paris. I expect of you more force of character. They tell me that you weep continually. Fie! How unbecoming that is.
tweets.nap-18070119-04: My love, I am in the receipt of your letter. I have smiled at your fear for my safety. I am in despair at the tone of your letters, and at what I hear of you. I forbid you to weep, to be melancholy and anxious; I wish that you may be cheerful, amiable, and happy.
tweets.nap-18070203-94: My Friend, there was a great battle yesterday; I gained the victory, but we have lost a great many men. The loss of the enemy, which is still more considerable, does not console me.
tweets.nap-18070205-93: My Cousin, I am in pursuit of the Russian army. I have driven it from all its positions, and am going to force it back behind the Niemen. It is splendid weather, and everything is going on well.
tweets.nap-18070209-215: My love, there was a great battle yesterday. Victory remains with me, but I have lost many men. The loss of the enemy, still more considerable, does not console me. I write these few lines myself, though greatly fatigued, to tell you that I am well, and that I love you.
tweets.nap-18070211-216: I send you one line, my love. You must have been very anxious. I have beaten the enemy in a memorable battle, but it has cost me many brave men. The inclement weather constrains me to return to my cantonments. Do not indulge in grief, I entreat you. All this will soon end.
tweets.nap-18070212-06: I send you a letter from General Darmagnac; he is a very good soldier, who commanded the thirty-second. He is much attached to me. If this Madame de Richemont is rich, and it would be a good match, I should see the marriage with pleasure. Introduce them to each other.
tweets.nap-18070214-217: My love, I linger at Eylau. The land lies strewn with dead and wounded, war's ugly face. Hearts break at such victims. I am well. I did what I came for: the foe recoils, his designs abandoned. A thousand kisses.
tweets.nap-18070218-07: I write you two words. I am very well. I am in movement to put my army into winter quarters. It rains and thaws as in the month of. We have not yet had one cold day. Adieu, my love. Entirely thine.
tweets.nap-18070228-96: I spread the following reports in an official manner. They are, however, true.
tweets.nap-18070302-218: My love, it is two or three days since I have written to you. I reproach myself for it, for I know your anxiety. I am very well. My affairs are moving prosperously. I am in a miserable village, where I must still remain for some time. This is not like being in a great city.
tweets.nap-18070302-97: My Son, I congratulate you on the confinement of the princess; I am very anxious to learn that she is doing well and out of all danger. I hope that your daughter will be as good and as amiable as her mother. It remains for you now to have a boy next year.
tweets.nap-18070313-08: I learn, my love, that the mischievous talk which was held in your saloon, at Mayence, is renewed. Silence it. I shall be much displeased if you do not find a remedy for this. You allow yourself to be afflicted by the remarks of those who ought to comfort you.
tweets.nap-18070314-100: I have seen in the newspapers a pretended letter written in Russia. It is lamentable. We do not require to be defended by fables. No man in his senses will be deceived, and it will only create a bad effect.
tweets.nap-18070317-09: It is not right for you to go with humble equipage to the minor theatres. That is not suitable to your rank. You ought only to go to the large theatres in imposing state. Live as you were accustomed to do when I was in Paris. My health is very good.
tweets.nap-18070322-102: I there can be no doubt that rear-admiral allemand should not attack an equal force of the enemy, much more a superior force.
tweets.nap-18070325-103: Did I ever give you an order to send 10,000 Prussians to Spain? I told my Minister for Foreign affairs to make such a proposal to Spain, but was that equivalent to an order from me? This sort of thing has happened several times.
tweets.nap-18070401-106: I am delighted to hear nothing more of Madame de Stael. When I trouble myself about her it is when I have facts before me. That woman is a regular crow; she thought that she saw the tempest coming. Let her go to Her Lake Leman. To Cambaceres: There is nothing new here.
tweets.nap-18070402-10: My love, I write you a word. I have removed my headquarters to a very pleasant chateau, something like that of Bessieres, where I have many fire-places. This is very grateful to me, as I rise often in the night. I love to see the fire. My health is perfect.
tweets.nap-18070404-104: My Son, send General Lauriston twenty-five gold and silver watches to be given to the Turks. Also send twenty-five to Marmont. You say that you have 20,000 men with the grand army. You do not believe this yourself. You have only 10,000; and what men!
tweets.nap-18070414-105: I must say that I was not pleased with the preamble of your order for suppressing the monasteries. With regard to all that concerns religion you must use the language of religion, and not that of philosophy. That is the great art of the person who governs.
tweets.nap-18070418-11: I have your letter of the of. I see with pain that you are chagrined at what I said to you. As usual, your little Creole head becomes excited and afflicted. Let us then say no more about it. I am very well.
tweets.nap-18070501-107: The aides-de-camp of Marshal Augereau, instead of remaining with the army, have followed him to Paris. Let me know to what corps they belong, for it is not my intention to allow them to remain in Paris. They might say more than was agreeable about Eylau.
tweets.nap-18070501-108: It seems to me that I wrote to the Princess Pauline that she might go to the waters. I only opposed this by way of advice, because I see that the doctors order waters when they want to get rid of their patients.
tweets.nap-18070510-12: I have received your letter. I do not understand what you tell me about ladies in correspondence with me. I love none but my little Josephine, good, pouting, and capricious, who knows how to quarrel with grace, as she does every thing else.
tweets.nap-18070510-81: I can conceive all the grief which the death of the little Napoleon must cause you.
tweets.nap-18070512-13: I received your letter; you lean toward St Cloud. I grieve at Madame's misconduct. Can you not urge her to mend? Such ways will soon bring grave quarrels with her husband.
tweets.nap-18070514-14: I can appreciate the grief which the death of poor Napoleon must cause you. You can understand the anguish which I experience. I could wish that I were with you, that you might become moderate and discreet in your grief. You have had the happiness of never losing any children.
tweets.nap-18070516-15: I have received your letter of the of. I see in it already the injury which you are suffering; and I fear that you are not reasonable, and that you afflict yourself too much from the calamity which has befallen us. Adieu, my love. Entirely thine.
tweets.nap-18070520-16: I have received your letter of the of. I see that you have gone to Lucken. I think that you may rest there a fortnight. That will give much pleasure to the Belgians, and will serve to divert your mind. I see with pain that you are not wise.
tweets.nap-18070526-17: I have received your letter and am glad Hortense has reached Lucken. I am grieved by her continued distress. She must show more courage and composure.
tweets.nap-18070602-109: My Friend, I have just seen the Emperor Alexander; I was well satisfied with him; he is a handsome, good, and youthful Emperor; he has more intelligence than is generally supposed. He is coming to stay at Tilsit tomorrow.
tweets.nap-18070602-110: I have just seen the Emperor of Russia in the middle of the Niemen on a raft where a handsome flag was hoisted. Tomorrow the Emperor is going to present the king of Prussia to me, and is coming to reside here. To that effect I have neutralised the town of Tilsit.
tweets.nap-18070606-18: I am very well, my love. Your Letter of yesterday gave me much pain. It appears that you are continually sad and that you are not reasonable. The weather is very bad. Adieu, my love; I love you and desire to hear that you are cheerful and contented.
tweets.nap-18070622-111: While waiting for St. Denis to be ready, have the body of the little Napoleon placed in a chapel at Notre Dame. On the same day, in a proclamation to the army, I said: Frenchmen, you are worthy of yourselves and of me.
tweets.nap-18070624-191: Soldiers, early this month the Russians struck our cantonments, mistaking my stillness. Too late they learned my rest was a lion's. They rue disturbing it. Friedland stands worthy sister to Marengo, Austerlitz, Jena. I salute you.
tweets.nap-18070625-113: Let me know if there are any muskets at Koenigsberg. I was told that there were 160,000, and since then I hear nothing more about them. As I have announced this fact everywhere, I shall be very angry if I have been deceived.
tweets.nap-18070625-219: My love, I have just come from an interview with the Emperor Alexander. He is a very handsome, amiable, and youthful emperor. He has more ability than is generally supposed. Tomorrow he takes his lodgings in the city of Tilsit. Adieu, my love.
tweets.nap-18070701-81: The day after you reach Paris, tell Portugal: shut every port to England by early autumn or I declare war and seize English goods. Press Madrid the same day through the Prince of Peace.
tweets.nap-18070714-114: Sir, my Brother, desirous of placing near your Majesty some one who will be able to express to you viva voce the sentiments with which you have inspired me, I send you my aide-de-camp, the general of Division, Savary, whom I have appointed ambassador to your court.
tweets.nap-18070718-26: My love, I arrived yesterday, at five o'clock in the evening, at Dresden, in very good health, although I have been a hundred hours in the carriage without leaving it. I am here at the house of the king of Saxony, with whom I am very much pleased.
tweets.nap-18070722-115: I write to m. Alquier to present a note in which he will insist on the number of French cardinals being forty. The Russians ill-treat the poor as well as the rich. They plunder, burn villages, and massacre -- these are their amusements.
tweets.nap-18070802-116: If England spurns Russian mediation, Denmark must declare on her, or I declare on Denmark. Then seize the whole Danish mainland. Cry loudly that Denmark opened the Sound and let the sea be violated, waters Danes should hold inviolable as their soil. Bernadotte, I rely on you.
tweets.nap-18070804-117: I do not know what rash act you suppose the Pope to be capable of committing. You should have sent some troops in the direction of Bologna, and if he commits an imprudence it will be a fine opportunity for depriving him of the Roman states.
tweets.nap-18070810-118: I am proprietor, in the duchy of Warsaw, of all the debts due to the king of Prussia by private individuals. These debts are due for money advanced to proprietors on the security of their land. They appear to amount to a sum of 60,000,000 francs.
tweets.nap-18070826-119: The English have disembarked at Copenhagen. They are bombarding that town. My opinion is that Russia should march an army against Sweden to force her to take part with Denmark. The Emperor Alexander has only to say what he desires and I will do all that is necessary.
tweets.nap-18070922-120: DeLima (Portuguese ambassador) went yesterday to see the Grand Duke of Berg (Murat) without having been presented to that prince, which was his duty, for three reasons -- because he is my brother-in-law, because he is grand admiral, and because he is a reigning prince.
tweets.nap-18070924-121: I write to Marshal Victor to inform General Blucher that if he makes any preparations for war, and if he does not cease his bragging, he will send troops to besiege him in Kolberg; that this is the formal order of the Emperor, who is tired of the Prussian fanfaronnades.
tweets.nap-18070925-122: Send for M. Izquierdo to-morrow, and confer with him about the money which the king of Spain owes me, the affairs of Portugal, and those of Etruria.
tweets.nap-18071007-123: I order an extraordinary courier to Junot: within a day of receipt let him march into Spain for Portugal.
tweets.nap-18071014-124: Send me each province described: roads, ground, sketches by my engineers, distances, country, resources. Never quit your army: a general is great only with it, small at court. Portugal's war on England does not suffice; march on. I suspect English intrigue behind you.
tweets.nap-18071101-125: Marescalchi will communicate to you the treaty which I have concluded with Spain; you will see that Tuscany belongs to me. My intention is to unite it to Italy. I think that I have troops enough at Leghorn to accomplish this.
tweets.nap-18071115-192: I since America suffers her vessels to be searched, she adopts the principle that the flag does not cover the goods.
tweets.nap-18071201-126: I saw Lucien at Mantua. I think he promised to send me his eldest daughter. This young person must be in Paris by. Lucien, who appeared to be swayed by conflicting feelings, had not the strength of mind to come to a decision.
tweets.nap-18071211-19: My love, yours pleased me, especially your joy in the Garden of Plants. I stand at my journey's far end; I may soon reach Paris, where nothing will delight me like seeing you.
tweets.nap-18080301-81: Is maple sugar from Berlin true, and turnip sugar sound? Inquire for me. I brought France to beet sugar, though Swiss tea never matched China leaf, nor chicory true coffee, in French mouths. Five hundred works now boil beet.
tweets.nap-18080327-128: My Brother, the king of Spain has just abdicated; the prince of the peace has been thrown into prison; an insurrection has broken out at Madrid. The Grand Duke of Berg was obliged to enter the city with 40,000 men. Up to the present the people call lustily for me.
tweets.nap-18080401-129: I have received your different letters on the subject of the language used by the various ambassadors in Paris. I can hardly believe that Count Tolstoy made use of the language attributed to him; it is a Parisian quolibet.
tweets.nap-18080401-131: I have received your letter with those of the queen of Naples, of Charlotte, and Zenaide (Joseph's daughter). I reached Bayonne yesterday. The Infant Don Carlos is here also, but I have not seen him, as he fell ill on the evening of my arrival.
tweets.nap-18080412-130: I approve of your march and all that you have done. I have made known my intentions to five or six grandees who accompany the prince.
tweets.nap-18080416-220: I have arrived here in good health, a little fatigued by the route which is melancholy and very rough. I am very glad that you stopped, for the houses here are very bad and very small. I am, today, to go to a small house in the country, half a league distant from the city.
tweets.nap-18080423-221: My love, Hortense mothers another son. My joy is complete. I marvel not at your silence: you wrote before she was brought to bed. Kiss her for me.
tweets.nap-18080501-133: I find the Spanish ambassador complaint ridiculous: the papers deny Charles was forced to abdicate.
tweets.nap-18080501-134: Tell Laforest I rue my ambassador's softness. Enlighten Berg, don't flatter him; balance him, don't follow his follies. Junta and Castille outwit my lieutenant; ignorant of the renunciations, they hesitate, voiceless for Murat, drowned in hate and shame.
tweets.nap-18080503-132: I congratulate you on the birth of a son. I wish the prince to be called Charles Napoleon. The child was christened Charles Louis Napoleon.
tweets.nap-18080602-193: Second self, after having secured for you a constitution which may establish the sacred and salutary authority of the sovereign, with the liberties and privileges of the people. Spaniards: Reflect on what your fathers were; I...
tweets.nap-18080603-135: Several artistes have fled from Paris, and taken refuge at St. Petersburg. I beg that you will ignore this bad conduct. We have no lack of ballet girls and actresses in Paris.
tweets.nap-18080707-136: I send your Majesty the constitution which the Spanish Junta has drawn up. The disorder in this country had reached a pitch difficult to conceive. In the new situation Spain will, in reality, be more independent of me than ever.
tweets.nap-18080810-137: I have received an extraordinary courier from Caulaincourt. Alexander says he will help if Austria makes war and is concerned about Spain.
tweets.nap-18080910-139: Caulaincourt says you leave for Erfurth shortly. I send Lannes to meet you on the Vistula, foretasting our meeting. To Soult: mark the papers on Stein. I demand his dismissal or Prussia's king stays exiled; I seized his Westphalian lands. Austria wants no war. I count on Russia.
tweets.nap-18080914-138: Madam, my Sister, I am delighted with the return of your Majesty to Berlin, which realises my dearest wishes. It will depend only on the king and your Majesty for our countries to resume the sentiments which existed previous to late events.
tweets.nap-18080929-222: I have a slight cold. I have received your letter from Malmaison. I am highly pleased here with the Emperor and with every one. It is one hour after midnight and I am fatigued. Adieu, my love. Take care of your health.
tweets.nap-18081001-141: My Friend, I have received your letter. I see with pleasure that you are in good health. I have just been shooting over the battle-field of Jena. We breakfasted at the spot where I bivouacked for the night. I was present at the ball of Weimar.
tweets.nap-18081002-140: I have no Englishmen in my service, and an Englishman of the Windham faction alone ought to be received in Holland. All the Frenchmen, either in your service, or merchants, complain of your ministry.
tweets.nap-18081009-20: I have received, my love, your letter. I see with pleasure that you are well. I have just come from a drive over the Battle-field of Jena. We breakfasted upon the spot where I passed the night in bivouac. I have been present at a ball in Weimar. The Emperor Alexander danced.
tweets.nap-18081014-142: I have concluded all my Affairs with the Emperor of Russia. I start to-morrow for Paris, and I shall be at Bayonne before a month. Send me a report on the exact situation of the army.
tweets.nap-18081101-143: I have just arrived here. Your Troops are too scattered. I recommend you to write to us twice a day so that I may know where my corps are. Having ridden at full gallop across the Landes I am tired.
tweets.nap-18081126-144: I have routed the armies of Andalusia, Aragon, Valencia, and New Castile at Tudela, taking their guns, baggage, and many prisoners.
tweets.nap-18081201-145: My Friend, I have been pursuing the English for several days, but they fly terrified. They have abandoned the debris of Romana's army so as not to lose half a day. Over a hundred baggage waggons have been taken.
tweets.nap-18081203-196: Vain you employ the name of the people. If you cannot find means to pacify them, it is because you yourselves excited them and misled them by falsehood.
tweets.nap-18090101-146: It is the custom of the pope to send tapers to different powers. You must write to my agent at Rome that I will not accept one. The king of Spain, too, does not want one. Write to Naples and to Holland to refuse them.
tweets.nap-18090101-147: My son, Battaglia brings word Augusta bore another princess. I hope a boy next. To Spain's king I wrote: enter Madrid in splendour, win the people, set councils and ministers swiftly to govern. Again I told him: the English flee, a money convoy taken. They are in full retreat.
tweets.nap-18090321-148: I have received your letter. War seems imminent. Assemble as many troops as possible to defend your country and support the common cause.
tweets.nap-18090401-197: I have defeated the enemy at Eckmühl, Peissing, Landshut, and Ratisbon. Our rapid marches and courage brought us 100 guns, 40 standards, and 50,000 prisoners.
tweets.nap-18090401-198: Ratisbon. One hundred pieces of cannon, forty standards, fifty thousand prisoners, three bridge equipages, three thousand baggage-wagons with their horses, and all the money chests of the regiments, are the fruits of the rapidity of your marches, and of your courage.
tweets.nap-18090418-223: I arrived here at four o'clock in the morning. I am leaving. Everything is in motion. Military operations are in great activity. Up to the present moment, there is nothing new. My health is good. Wholly thine.
tweets.nap-18090501-149: My Friend, I have received your letter. The bullet which touched me did not wound me. It barely shaved the tendon Achilles. My health is very good; you are wrong to feel uneasy. My affairs are going on well here. We have entered Vienna.
tweets.nap-18090501-199: Entering Vienna: within weeks of the foe crossing the Inn, the same day, the same hour, we entered Vienna. Their militia, mass levies, ramparts raised by Lorraine princes' impotent rage fell at your first sight. I watched my eagles plant themselves in the imperial capital.
tweets.nap-18090501-200: Hungarians, the hour to revive your freedom strikes. I offer peace, whole territory, constitutions inviolate, kept or renewed as the age demands. I ask nothing. Rise and take what I hold out.
tweets.nap-18090512-224: I have dispatched the brother of the Duchess of Montebello to inform you that I am master of Vienna, and that everything here is entirely prosperous. My health is very good.
