tweets.nap-18090519-150: You have greatly alarmed Paris about the affairs of Prussia. Even if it were true that she had attacked us, Prussia is of no consequence, and could be easily subdued. You have not shown yourself sufficiently prudent in this matter.
tweets.nap-18090601-152: I reply to your letter concerning Carnot and the unfortunate state of His Affairs. If he had merely helped to relieve Manberige he would have been entitled to my gratitude and interest. As minister of war he has a right to a pension.
tweets.nap-18090701-151: I send you news of my victories at Enzersdorf and Wagram. The enemy is fleeing in disorder; events are going as I hoped, and Eugene is well.
tweets.nap-18090701-154: I have received at the same time the two inclosed letters from General Miollis. I am sorry that the Pope was arrested; it was a great piece of folly. Cardinal Pacca should have been arrested and the Pope allowed to remain quietly at Rome.
tweets.nap-18090710-155: You know my Tyrol design. Stand at Innsbruck by high summer. No vain proclamations; be stern, disarm the land, seize hostages, make examples, and waste no hour. The mountaineers burn to throw off the hated Bavarian yoke and rejoin Austria. I will break them.
tweets.nap-18090714-153: I have received your Majesty’s letter. I had already thanked you for the friendship you showed by sending troops against Schill.
tweets.nap-18090722-156: Liechtenstein delivered your letter naming your negotiators. I empower Champagny likewise. If this fourth peace after Campo Formio, Luneville, Presburg proves lasting, shielding the continent from English plots, I call it a blessed hour.
tweets.nap-18090801-157: You send no Spanish news. The king writes Wellesley reached Talavera with twenty-five thousand English and joined Cuesta. Soult's clumsy march missed him, deplorable. I hope the king, fifty-five thousand strong, bars Madrid and calls Soult in.
tweets.nap-18090818-158: I send you the despatches from St. Petersburg. There is nothing new. However, you will remark that there is always something obscure as regards the wishes of that cabinet.
tweets.nap-18090826-225: I received your letter from Malmaison. I have heard that you are fleshy, fresh, and blooming. I assure you that Vienna is not an interesting city. I wish very much to be at Paris. Adieu, my love. I go to the play twice a week. It is quite common-place. It whiles away the evening.
tweets.nap-18090901-159: You have no confidence in Abbe de Pradt. I do not know if I told you to distrust that man as the greatest enemy that we can have.
tweets.nap-18090901-160: By every Trafalgar account Dumanoir disobeyed signals, honour and duty: never freed our centre, never closed with the foe, sheered off while still able to fight. With our returned prisoner-officers flooding home, I order his conduct judged. Cowardice afloat disgraces my flag.
tweets.nap-18090909-21: My love, I arrived here yesterday at two o'clock in the morning: I came in order to see my troops. My health was never better. I know that you are well. I shall be in Paris at a moment when nobody expects me. Everything goes well here, and to my satisfaction. Adieu, my love.
tweets.nap-18091028-161: I beg that you will write me an historical sketch tending to prove that the popes have always been the enemies of the power predominating in Italy.
tweets.nap-18091122-162: I see with pleasure that you have arrived at Milan. You have written a work on your Italian campaign. I beg you will send it to me. I have found my financial affairs here in great disorder. The English expedition cost me 2,000,000 francs.
tweets.nap-18100117-100: My love, D'Audenarde, whom I sent to you this morning, informs me that you have no more fortitude since you have been at Malmaison. And yet that place is full of our affection which will not and can not ever change, at least on my part.
tweets.nap-18100207-81: You furnish me with no report respecting the administration of the theatres, and you have new pieces rehearsed without informing me. I learn that the Mort d'Abel and a ballet are being rehearsed. You should not have any new piece rehearsed without my consent.
tweets.nap-18100322-01: I have read with interest the details of the ceremonies which took place at Vienna.
tweets.nap-18100403-02: I do not consider it right that you should issue a proclamation to your People.
tweets.nap-18100421-101: My love, yours pains me by its style. I never change; my heart is constant. What Eugene told you, I know not. Trust me and write kindly.
tweets.nap-18100428-22: My love, both your letters are here. I write Eugene. Tascher weds the Leyen princess by my order. Tomorrow I see my Antwerp flotilla and works. I return mid next month. Be patient and love me.
tweets.nap-18100516-03: Caulaincourt has informed me of all the amiable things which your Majesty has said on the subject of my marriage. I beg you to accept my thanks. My feelings towards you are as unchangeable as the political principles which govern the relations of my empire.
tweets.nap-18100610-102: I have received your letter. I see with pain the danger through which you have passed. For an inhabitant of the isles of the ocean to perish in a lake -- that had been a fatality. The queen is better, and I hope that her health will soon be restored.
tweets.nap-18100620-04: Prince Kourakine has handed me the letter which your Majesty has been good enough to write in order to congratulate me on my marriage.
tweets.nap-18100701-05: You will receive from the office of the secretary of state a decree annulling that which appointed Fouche to the government of Rome. Inform General Miollis that it is my intention to leave him at the post which he fulfils so well, and that I reckon upon his zeal.
tweets.nap-18100708-23: My love, yours received. You will have seen Eugene, and his presence will have done you good, I am sure. The waters agree with you, to my joy. Keep them a while.
tweets.nap-18100720-103: I have received, my love, your letter of the of. I see with pleasure that the waters have done you good, and that you like Geneva. I think that you will do well to remain there several weeks. My health is pretty good. The conduct of the king of Holland grieves me.
tweets.nap-18100726-06: My brother and dear father, yours received. I thank you for its kind words. Metternich, Schwartzenberg and your subjects in Paris through our sad days earned my warm praise; I ask your leave to grant several my Legion.
tweets.nap-18100802-07: I cannot allow Prince Kourakine to leave without reiterating to him my feelings towards your Imperial majesty.
tweets.nap-18100914-104: My love, yours tells me you are well, joy to me. The Empress, four months gone, thrives and loves me dearly. The little Napoleons flourish at the Italian pavilion in St Cloud park.
tweets.nap-18100917-08: I exactions of all kinds are committed in Spain, and a traffic is made of the liberation of prisoners. Send an officer with a letter to General Kellermann. Write at the same time to Massena to have the individuals guilty of these crimes arrested.
tweets.nap-18100920-09: Sunday I review in Paris: the Portuguese at Meaux, a Spanish rear battalion, the Dutch Guard, my French Guard. Mine feast every Portuguese private; yours feast their officers. I bind brave foes to me with honour and roast meat.
tweets.nap-18101001-10: I beg that you will continue to take measures for procuring me all the works published in England, either concerning my policy or on the affairs of the day. I derive very important intelligence from them.
tweets.nap-18101002-105: I have received your letter. Hortense will tell you what I think. Visit your son this winter, then return to the waters of Aix next year or spend the spring at Navarre.
tweets.nap-18101104-11: Send my mother a passport for Louis to live where he will in south France or Italy. To my marine minister: forward a thousand Russian-bought masts to Dantzic. Dantzic is mine, French rule, French garrison, whatever Tilsit paper says of free towns.
tweets.nap-18101114-106: My love, I have received your letter. Hortense has spoken to me of you. I see with pleasure that you are contented. Hortense was a woman of very superior accomplishments.
tweets.nap-18110108-107: I have received your New Year letter and thank you for your kind words. I am glad you are content. My health is very good, though I have not been out for a fortnight.
tweets.nap-18110322-108: My love, I have received your letter. I thank you. My son is stout and very well. I hope that he will be prospered, qu'il viendra a bien. He has my chest, my mouth, and eyes. I hope that he will fulfill his destiny. I am always well pleased with Eugene.
tweets.nap-18110607-12: Lay Belliard's letter before me no more; he writes mad. Resigning rather than obeying is disobedience, punishable by death. His three thousand foot and twelve hundred horse could have saved the south. Such paragraphs shame a soldier; I would have him seized and made example.
tweets.nap-18110802-13: I send you extracts from the English journals. You must show them to Prince Kourakine while conversing with him. After this you must send them to Comte Lauriston, so that he may show them in Russia.
tweets.nap-18110816-14: Which is the best port for assembling my squadron of the ocean? I see only two between which to choose -- Brest or Cherbourg. Which of those two ports offers the greatest facilities for invading England or Ireland?
tweets.nap-18110822-16: I beg that you will have the fortifications of Geneva blown up. Perhaps in a military point of view it would be of interest to keep this place; but, the inhabitants having always exhibited a bad feeling, I have decided upon blowing up the fortifications without delay.
tweets.nap-18110823-15: The Boulogne flotilla limped home damaged; I think a gunboat foundered. Write my crews: no gloom, such gales are their school. To Berthier: shame on Soult for sending Albuera flags by a foreigner, an Austrian turncoat who fought us. Ridiculous.
tweets.nap-18110901-18: I have received your letter concerning the cheating of Bourrienne at Hamburg. It will be important to throw light upon what he has done. Have the Jew, Gumprecht Mares, arrested, seize his papers, and place him in solitary confinement.
tweets.nap-18110903-17: I beg that you will pay 2,500 francs a month to the ex-queen of Etruria, at her convent in Rome. The poor queen of Etruria, deprived of her kingdom, which was handed over by me to my Sister Eliza, was most cruelly treated.
tweets.nap-18111101-19: I return you the letters from Savona.
tweets.nap-18111231-20: I have seen the porcelain service sent to the Empress as a New Year’s gift. It is ugly; make the next one more attractive, with portraits of the Empress and my sisters on each cup.
tweets.nap-18120307-21: It will be necessary to send a courier to Comte Lauriston to-day. Do not speak to him about the espionage of Czernitchef, of which you are supposed to know nothing at present.
tweets.nap-18120406-22: I return you the letters of your Brother. Reply that cacao, sugar, and coffee are not English merchandise, and ought not to be burned. What ought to be burned are articles of English manufacture.
tweets.nap-18120616-23: I write to Marshal Ney that his corps is diverging from the route traced out for it, and commits devastation everywhere.
tweets.nap-18120618-81: I similar suspicions attach to the conduct of the captain of the danae who might have helped the Rivoli. The conduct of the post captain who was at lorient is sharply criticised; it is said that he might have succoured the two frigates. Make a report on these two affairs.
tweets.nap-18120701-25: Write to Marshal Ney that the situation of his army corps seems to me very alarming as regards his artillery. Without artillery his corps would be greatly compromised.
tweets.nap-18120702-24: Davoust fought at Mohilef; details still out. Bagration tried to ride over him and broke. An evening field-note says the foe beaten. Today our van took eight guns and seven hundred men. Russia lies at Vitebsk. Keep this to yourself; write nothing. Great events ripen.
tweets.nap-18120801-28: I have received your Calculation of Probabilities with pleasure. There was a time when I should have read it with interest; to-day I must confine myself to expressing the satisfaction which I experience every time that I see you bring out new works.
tweets.nap-18120802-26: I have received the portrait of the king, and find it very like him. It furnishes me with an opportunity, of which I avail myself with pleasure, of expressing my satisfaction with the care you take of him.
tweets.nap-18120807-27: I beg that you will see if the two or three hundred carts left behind at Wilna, exposed to the air, have been placed under cover in a church or an arsenal. If that has not yet been done the governor should see to it.
tweets.nap-18120829-29: We reached Viazma; the foe still melts toward Moscow. I wait word of two Russian divisions marching from Moldavia. I begged Austria to stiffen Schwartzenberg's horse with three thousand to cover his losses.
tweets.nap-18120907-91: Borodino: soldiers, the battle you craved is come. Victory rests with you; we need it. It brings full winter quarters and swift homecoming. I ask the impossible no longer, strike!
tweets.nap-18120920-92: Monsieur my brother: learning your Cassel minister's brother lingers in Moscow, I sent for him and spoke long. I bid him carry you my mind. War wastes both empires; I still prefer an understanding. Hear me through him.
tweets.nap-18121001-30: I repeat: Marchand gathers all sick and wounded to Mojafsk abbey with every cart and carriage; staff sees it done.
tweets.nap-18121107-31: I have just passed the Beresina, but the ice floating down that river makes the bridges very unstable. The army which was opposed to Schwartzenberg wished to dispute the passage; tonight it is concentrated on the right bank of the river at Borisoff.
tweets.nap-18121201-34: You must go to Berlin, and before leaving Wilna let me know how things are looking. You will find at Berlin a letter for the king of Prussia, and my instructions for yourself. You must wait at Berlin for orders and write to me every day. 266 Polish lancers formed his escort.
tweets.nap-18121210-33: I have received your letter. The Moniteur reports little of importance on Spain. Burgos’s resistance is a fine military feat, but fortresses cannot be taken without siege guns.
tweets.nap-18121214-32: I pause at Dresden to write you. Despite fatigue my health never was better. I left Lithuania after Beresina, leaving the Grand army to the king of Naples. In four days I reach Paris for the most urgent affairs.
tweets.nap-18130101-35: I received your letter. I see the army command in your hands with pleasure. I find the king of Naples extravagant; little more and I would have him arrested as an example. He is brave in Battle but devoid of combinations and moral courage. Employ Ney; you will need him.
tweets.nap-18130126-36: All your efforts must preserve Warsaw. Reports show the Russians on the Beresina thought themselves lost; but for Partouneaux wandering into their lines, Victor would have beaten them as we beat the admiral and crushed them.
tweets.nap-18130302-37: I received your letter from Leipsic. Send me news of Morand, even rumours. After York's treason, Prussia will not stay our ally long, though the issue is still undecided. I do not think she has as many troops as Regnier.
tweets.nap-18130312-38: It is unfortunate you do not see Magdeburg can only live by requisitions, authorised by war and practised since the world began; Italy in my last campaign, even Strasburg and Mayence lived so. Why not do for Magdeburg what I did for Mayence? Instead of energy you undo all.
tweets.nap-18130426-39: I do not intend you to send your police memoranda straight to the Empress. It has no advantage and many objections. She is too young to have her mind corrupted or disturbed by police details. Address such papers to me alone.
tweets.nap-18130504-40: Knowing your joy in my fortune, I announce Lutzen, which Providence gave my arms. Though I ordered all under fire myself, I came through untouched and hale. I hear daily from the Empress, my prime minister, to my full content.
tweets.nap-18130507-43: Send the enclosed to Serra at Prague. We reached Dresden; tomorrow the army crosses in pursuit. Tell Senft that to offend the confederation is war against me; my friendship made me patient till now, but the crisis lets you grant Saxony only six hours for satisfaction.
tweets.nap-18130510-41: We reached Dresden; I hold both banks and the Elbe strongholds. Likely I march into Silesia. Long disgraced, Fouche now gets my secret summons: as I enter Prussia I will set him over its government. Lutzen drove the foe over the river; let him come at once. Only the Regent knows.
tweets.nap-18130512-42: I gave battle to the Russo-Prussian army entrenched at Bautzen and Hochkirch, and Providence granted me victory. I tell you my health is excellent, counting on your interest.
tweets.nap-18130531-44: The Swedes having entered Hamburg, send me at once a declaration of war against Sweden. Their insolence must be answered without delay.
tweets.nap-18130531-45: I direct you: should the case of the queen of Sicily arise, treat her with the honours of her rank and utmost consideration; she is the Empress's grandmother and an unfortunate queen persecuted by the English.
tweets.nap-18130601-46: I saw with pleasure that amid political storms your feelings stayed unchangeable. Sweden's ill will comes from my refusal to join the spoliation of Norway.
tweets.nap-18130717-47: I hold the Bishop of Nantes the most enlightened priest of the empire, the finest Doctor of the Sorbonne. None was more steeped in the Gospel; none better honoured sovereigns' rights while rejecting Rome's monstrous abuses, which shed so much blood and schisms in ignorant days.
tweets.nap-18130801-50: Present me a plan for gratifying my actors, and tell Turenne to send them back to France by the twelfth. I wrote Savary on the crisis; see him. I hope to make Austria repent her folly and treason. Likely the foe denounces the armistice and Austria declares war on us.
tweets.nap-18130801-51: My minister will have told you Austria declared war. Her manifesto is empty; plainly she seizes the hour to recover influence. The Prague talks never happened; envoys never met. Spanish hopes and English intrigue did the rest. We fight soon.
tweets.nap-18130807-49: I told you Oudinot with Vandamme, Regnier and Padoue, eighty thousand men, debouches by Luckau and Bayreuth when the armistice breaks, to stand days from Berlin.
tweets.nap-18130817-48: I long thought Caulaincourt and Narbonne Let Metternich's honeyed style dupe them. The Austro-Russian terms were settled last winter, and I am sure the conditions for me were signed then.
tweets.nap-18130825-109: I received your letter. I see with pleasure that you are in good health. I spent days at Trianon and my health is good. Take care of yourself and write often. I think of you and send my love.
tweets.nap-18130826-52: I told you my plans yesterday. The whole foe appeared before Dresden and St Cyr feared attack; I go there myself. To divert them, debouch at once and fall on their rear today, crushing the division watching you.
tweets.nap-18130830-53: Alexander's host lies utterly beaten. I took thirty thousand men, scores of guns, thirty colours; twelve thousand wounded strew the villages. Vandamme smashed Wurtemberg's Russians and marches on. Austria's new levies melt half-naked and shoeless after days afield.
tweets.nap-18130901-55: Macdonald stands at Gorlitz; should he keep retiring I must aid him. The disaster to the first corps was unforeseeable: Vandamme posted no sentry and kept no reserve.
tweets.nap-18130902-54: Write Ney: Oudinot rashly ventured near Wittenberg, so Tauentzien and Cossack clouds cut Macdonald's communications. Few have less brains. march to Bayreuth by the sixth; thence three marches from Berlin, our link restored, and the capital can be struck within days.
tweets.nap-18131031-56: I arrived here. Sixty thousand Bavarians and Austrians at Hanau tried to cut me from France. I gave them a drubbing, taking guns, standards and six thousand prisoners. My health never was better; I go to Mayence.
tweets.nap-18131110-57: The English push on Bayonne opened my frontier; they already landed goods near St Jean de Luz. I suppose you moved your customs line; this deserves your attention. Bavaria urges Eugene to desert me as she did herself, but he reported and rejected it. I see Austria's hand.
tweets.nap-18131110-58: Burn Marracq castle and all my houses there should the English come, so they never sleep in my bed. To Fouche: hasten to Naples and press the king to march to the Po; tell the queen too, and keep the land from Austria's false promises and vile tongue. I doubt him deeply.
tweets.nap-18140102-59: I marched on St Dizier, held by the foe, and drove them out, taking guns and prisoners. Blucher with twenty-five thousand men reached Brienne today. I cut his communications, occupied Bar, and now pursue him. If he stands we fight at Brienne on the morrow.
tweets.nap-18140110-60: Garrison every place; recall Sebastiani and your horse for the Meuse, turning Blucher's right toward Namur. Marmont wheels round Metz; Ney and Victor bar the Vosges; Mortier holds Langres.
tweets.nap-18140201-61: What! Hours after your Spanish drafts arrived, still not afield! Brief rest sufficed me: I won Nangis with dragoons fresh from Spain who never unbridled. You plead your Nismes battalions want clothes and drill, poor excuses!
tweets.nap-18140202-62: The allies set the Chatillon congress to open within days: Cathcart for London, Stadion for Austria, Humboldt for Prussia, Razoumovsky for Russia. I shall be at Troyes tomorrow. To Caulaincourt: the foe behaves vilely; villagers flee to the woods.
tweets.nap-18140206-63: I marvel Suchet never sent the Lyons Troops I demanded; they should be here and I hear nothing. If he disobeyed on his own head he is most culpable. To Joseph I wrote: I meant to strike Alexander at Bar and beat him, but false moves spoiled it.
tweets.nap-18140207-66: I note your gains with pleasure; had they been more decisive we could have kept Italy. I crushed the Silesian army and began beating Schwartzenberg. In days I took tens of thousands of prisoners, generals, hundreds of officers and scores of guns.
tweets.nap-18140210-64: I just reached Nogent. After Montereau the foe fell back on Troyes in bulk; only frost letting them march cross-country saved their baggage and guns. At Montereau, Bray and Nogent they committed unspeakable horrors; Let Paris know. Austria's Emperor never left Troyes.
tweets.nap-18140214-65: I send word of Vauchamps. Blucher, cut off at Vertus, joined Kleist and a fresh Russian corps, twenty thousand men, and marched on Etoges while Marmont fell back.
tweets.nap-18140220-67: Bassano sends you the allied proposals. You will see your sermons are misplaced; I need no preaching to sign an honourable peace if possible. He sends too an intercepted Angouleme letter.
tweets.nap-18140303-68: Before fortifying Paris the plan must be settled; yours is too tangled, I demand simplicity. Complaints reach me that mayors and bourgeois stop the people defending themselves. I see the same in Paris.
tweets.nap-18140310-71: The army I beat at Craonne was Russian. It lost heavily and fell back on Laon, joined by Bulow, York and Kleist forming the Prussian army. Laon favours them; yesterday I only observed it. This army threatens Paris more than Schwartzenberg's. I move toward Soissons.
tweets.nap-18140314-69: I reached Rheims, held by St Priest with three Russian divisions and a Prussian one fresh from Stettin. I beat them, retook the town, twenty guns, much baggage, five thousand prisoners. St Priest is mortally wounded, struck, remarkably, by the same gunner who killed Moreau.
tweets.nap-18140315-70: Mortier writes the foe retreats in good order on Laon; I sent horse to follow. Send peasants to learn if they hold Craonne in force. Recruit the villages through the mayors, sending officers and men; many ruined peasants ask only to serve.
tweets.nap-18140320-72: Yesterday I crossed the Aube at Plancy and marched straight on Mery, carried by evening. Alexander was at Arcis; we nearly met face to face before he fled to Troyes, at once evacuated by his headquarters. The foe flies everywhere.
tweets.nap-18140323-73: Send a disguised gendarme to Metz, one to Bar, one to Nancy, with letters to the mayors. Tell them we march on the enemy's rear; the hour is come to rise as one, ring the tocsin, seize their commandants and agents, and fall on their convoys.
tweets.nap-18140404-95: The allied powers proclaim me the sole bar to peace in Europe. Faithful to my oath, I declare myself ready to leave the throne, to quit France, even to die for my country's welfare, inseparable from my son's rights and the Empress's regency. I make this sacrifice for France.
tweets.nap-18140405-90: Soldiers, yielding to the necessity that parts me from the brave French army, I carry the sure knowledge that you will justify, by the great services the country expects of you, the praise even our enemies cannot refuse you. I thank you for twenty years of glory.
tweets.nap-18140420-96: Soldiers of my Old Guard, I bid you farewell. For twenty years I marched with you on the road to honour and glory. In these last days, as in our prosperity, you stood as models of courage and fidelity. I shall remember you always.
tweets.nap-18140610-74: I appoint the mayor of Porto Longone warden of my palace there: warden, keeper, master of the wardrobe and of the gardens, at six hundred francs. As the theatre must come down One day, I will spend nothing needless on it.
tweets.nap-18140826-75: I asked you to Tell Pauline to leave her piano master behind and bring only a good singer and songstress; we already have a fine violinist and pianist here. One of my mules drowned for want of a small stable pump; have a spare one mended. Send off Beausset's courier with my word.
tweets.nap-18140901-76: Tell Pauline I got all the Naples letters, and I am hurt mine reached her opened, as if I were a prisoner; I call such handling ridiculous and insulting. Thank Bertrand for the pamphlets, for and against; I will read them all one day.
tweets.nap-18150301-78: Plan me Soissons, La Fere, Chateau Thierry against surprise. Angouleme showed at Avignon; Paris events, I judge, forced him back. Spain at his rear still, his band must scatter.
tweets.nap-18150301-86: Frenchmen, Augereau's defection gave Lyons undefended to the foe. The army I trusted to him could have beaten the Austrians and fallen on the rear of the wing menacing Paris.
tweets.nap-18150410-79: Strike Berthier, Marmont, Victor, Perignon, Augereau and Kellermann from my marshals' roll. Report to me so the penniless among them may have pensions. To Mollien: pay the five per cents due Borghese, Eliza and my House princes.
tweets.nap-18150424-80: Order every department to make a set number of pikes to a chosen pattern. They will serve where muskets and scythes run short. I look to you to see it done.
tweets.nap-18150426-81: Suchet stays at Lyons, or returns by courier if gone. I give him the Alps outright. Grouchy, once relieved, hastens to Paris. I raised four armies, North, Moselle, Rhine, Alps, with watching corps besides. If war calls me away, Paris stays in your hands.
tweets.nap-18150501-82: I grant Soult forty thousand francs as marshal and forty thousand as commander, six thousand monthly for staff and office, twenty thousand for travel, renewed as spent.
tweets.nap-18150527-83: The Guard may soon march, leaving Paris without troops. I want the National Guard officers commissioned before the Guard departs. If the Chambers condemn Austria’s conduct over the King of Rome, so much the better.
tweets.nap-18150601-81: Soldiers, though I must leave the brave French army, I carry the sure knowledge you will justify, by the great services the country expects, the praise even foes cannot refuse. Though absent I follow your march.
tweets.nap-18150601-84: Find here my cavalry orders. Grouchy commands all, with a chief of staff and guns chief; every unemployed general is at his call. Let him reach Laon by the fifth, review his regiments, organise them and serve out cartridges to take the field by the tenth.
tweets.nap-18150606-85: See two hundred guns in place at the gates and works of Paris by the twelfth, and tell me when the first naval guns arrive. For three months your trust gave me unbounded power; today my wish is for France all the liberty possible, for I know anarchy always breeds absolute rule.
tweets.nap-18150609-81: I rode from before dawn and now snatch a few hours' rest; at Midnight I ride again. We forced the Sambre at Charleroi, pushed halfway to Namur and Brussels, took fifteen hundred prisoners and six guns, and wiped out four Prussian regiments at little cost to us. I lost few men.
tweets.nap-18150614-89: I shift my headquarters to Beaumont tonight; Tomorrow I move on Charleroi against the Prussians, battle or retreat to follow. My Army is splendid, the weather fine, the country well disposed.
tweets.nap-18150614-97: Soldiers, this day joins Marengo and Friedland, which twice fixed Europe's fate. As after Austerlitz and Wagram, we were too generous then, trusting the oaths of princes whose thrones we spared. Today the same foes conspire again; I ask you to show them French arms unchanged.
tweets.nap-18150616-87: My bulletin told you yesterday's news. I move my headquarters to Fleurus and launch a wide turning movement. I mourn General Letort deeply. Seize the estates of the Ghent traitors with the king; such treason must pay.
tweets.nap-18150616-88: I am sending you my aide-de-camp, General Flahault, with urgent instructions. Grouchy marches on Sombreffe with the third and fourth infantry corps; I will lead my Guard to Fleurus, attack if I meet the enemy, and reconnoitre toward Gembloux before deciding by mid-afternoon.
tweets.nap-18150617-98: Belgians, the Hanoverians and confederation troops grieve to bear arms for princes who are justice's foes and the crushers of nations' rights. They know the coalition as insatiable. I come as your liberator; join your courage to mine.
tweets.nap-18150804-99: Aboard the Bellerophon: I am no prisoner but England's guest. Her captain urged me aboard, saying his government ordered him to receive me and my suite and carry us to England if I wished. I took him at his word and claim the hospitality due.
tweets.nap-18160101-11: Rostopchin named, I ventured that the colour given his patriotic deed had surprised me; he had won my sympathy, not my anger, and more, I had envied him. Facing ruin, I admire the man who burns his own capital rather than yield it.
tweets.nap-18160101-12: Blucher and Wellington were surprised; they saw nothing of my moves near their outposts. To strike their two armies I might turn either flank or pierce their centre. I chose the blow that promised most.
tweets.nap-18160101-13: Quatre Bras should have been seized at dawn and entrenched; Ney hesitated and lost eight hours. The prince of Orange with only nine thousand men held that vital ground till mid-afternoon. I count those lost hours among the costliest of the campaign.
tweets.nap-18160101-14: At Acre, I admit, my post in mid-Syria with twelve thousand men was a daring venture. Desaix at the far end of my line lay five hundred leagues off. I risked all on speed and shock, and nearly carried it.
tweets.nap-18160710-10: About mid-morning I walked unannounced into his room to take the air toward the wood, where the carriage picked us up. Long had I neglected that drive. We spoke freely as we rode, and I returned refreshed.
tweets.nap-18210501-03: Tell them the great Napoleon died in the most wretched state, lacking all, abandoned to himself and his glory. I bequeath my memory to my son and to France; may my last words carry my unbroken love for both.
tweets.nap-17900811-700: I have not assigned Fayoum, Minyeh, or Beny-Soueyf to your division. Leave their administration alone; it is not yours to direct.
tweets.nap-17900817-700: You answer to no one but me in the administration of this province. Treat any contrary orders from Desaix as void.
tweets.nap-17910502-700: I have asked for a four-day halt to hostilities with Venice, beginning tomorrow. Please have the necessary orders issued.
tweets.nap-17930819-700: I have sent twenty saddles back to the stores. Organize the province and prepare the landings without delay.
tweets.nap-17940228-700: I am setting up two batteries where the enemy can see them. Once they are ready, they should make the coast untenable for the opposing wing.
tweets.nap-17950724-700: I stayed silent because I had no good news for you, my friend. I did not want to write merely to disappoint you.
tweets.nap-17960321-700: I have received your letter and dined with your wife at General Schérer’s. I would be delighted to be of service to her.
tweets.nap-17960408-700: I am trying to understand the purpose of Moulin’s mission and will pursue the matter until it becomes clear.
tweets.nap-17960408-701: I trust your honour too much to believe you would take a course that brings bloodshed. Such a decision would disgrace you before Europe and your own army.
tweets.nap-17960414-700: I have not changed my assessment of the enemy’s intentions.
tweets.nap-17960415-703: Take the position between Biestro and Rocca-Vignale so you can support Augereau’s attack. Carry out the movement precisely.
tweets.nap-17960415-705: I want you to inspect Masséna’s posts, then return to headquarters and report whether the enemy is moving.
tweets.nap-17960416-700: I am sending the Executive Board my account of Montenotte and Millesimo; you will find the battle details there.
tweets.nap-17960416-702: I want a search made at Sassello; it could serve several purposes. Move the IV demi-brigade toward Savona by way of Sassello within the hour.
tweets.nap-17960417-705: Your dispatch and the Board’s earlier letter show me the care you have taken to carry out your orders. I expected no less of your patriotism.
tweets.nap-17960420-700: You will find two cannon and four cavalry regiments at Lapre and Lesegno. The next battalion will follow when it is raised.
tweets.nap-17960420-702: I am ordering Joubert toward Lesegno after midnight; he should leave as soon as the troops are assembled.
tweets.nap-17960424-700: The enemy has a hundred thousand men, but only thirty-four thousand infantry and thirty-five hundred cavalry are in the force I am facing.
tweets.nap-17960424-702: I am forwarding the general’s request for a ceasefire, along with the answer I gave him.
tweets.nap-17960424-703: I am sending Junot to present the flags we captured from the Austrian and Piedmontese armies in our recent battles.
tweets.nap-17960424-704: I am sending you the twenty-one flags we captured from the enemy. Stop the light-artillery company from being recalled; I need it for this campaign.
tweets.nap-17960424-705: I am exhausted by the strain of this work and cannot write more at present.
tweets.nap-17960426-701: I am sending you the order for the Fourteenth Demi-Brigade to march.
tweets.nap-17960427-701: In unforeseen circumstances, I was advised to let events guide the decision.
tweets.nap-17960428-701: I am sending you the King’s order for Coni’s garrison to return the place to the officer I appointed.
tweets.nap-17960428-702: I have already sent one division of my army in that direction.
tweets.nap-17960428-703: I have ordered Augereau to move to Chivesana as the enemy evacuates and crosses the Po.
tweets.nap-17960428-704: I have told Laharpe to alert you if the enemy is retreating, so you can take the road to Nizzadella-Paglia.
tweets.nap-17960429-703: I also need you to send four thousand men through the Aosta valley.
tweets.nap-17960505-701: I need you to handle this important matter at once; there is no time to lose.
tweets.nap-17960505-702: I will always be glad to show you the esteem and respect I feel for you.
tweets.nap-17960511-701: You can plan on my being in Milan. Count me there for every purpose that matters.
tweets.nap-17960511-702: We crossed the Po, defeated the enemy twice, and captured or killed three thousand men, along with their baggage, stores, and twenty cannon.
tweets.nap-17960513-704: I have received your report that the Duke of Parma accepted the armistice.
tweets.nap-17960514-700: I will soon move on Livorno and Rome to carry out the Directory’s plans.
tweets.nap-17960516-700: I am forwarding an exchange for 650,000 pounds banco, payable to the treasurer for foreign affairs.
tweets.nap-17960516-701: Milan’s interests are at risk if you insist on holding the fort any longer. I urge you to reconsider.
tweets.nap-17960518-704: I accept your proposal to spare Milan and refrain from hostile acts there. I have sent word through my chief of staff.
tweets.nap-17960520-700: I tell my soldiers: you swept down from the Apennines like a torrent. Italy has seen what your courage can do.
tweets.nap-17960520-701: I need you to send the escorts, trunks, and merchandise to Tortona without delay.
tweets.nap-17960521-701: I am dissatisfied with the artillery supply. My orders have not been carried out properly, and that must be corrected.
tweets.nap-17960521-703: I am pleased that Balbi, the Republic’s banker, has rewarded you with fifteen thousand pounds.
tweets.nap-17960524-704: I invite the scientists to meet and tell me what support they need to renew science and the arts.
tweets.nap-17960528-701: I order him to report directly to headquarters and be replaced.
tweets.nap-17960531-700: I am sending you the account of the action at Borghetto and our crossing of the Mincio.
tweets.nap-17960603-700: I have arrived in the city and will leave tomorrow morning.
tweets.nap-17960604-700: The French were insulted. I expect you to insist that the insult be repaired.
tweets.nap-17960607-701: I hope the armistice we concluded can become the first step toward peace.
tweets.nap-17960608-700: Your young cousin came to see me yesterday.
tweets.nap-17960608-701: I am asking you to treat this matter as vital to the army’s survival.
tweets.nap-17960609-700: I am waiting for your answer about the 1,800 provisions I asked you to place in Coni so we can withdraw the garrison.
tweets.nap-17960610-703: I want every member of Pavia’s former municipality who has been arrested brought to trial.
tweets.nap-17960611-700: We are accustomed to freeing the places we reach.
tweets.nap-17960614-700: I will cross your territory, brave Tyroleans, to compel the Vienna court to make a peace Europe and its people need.
tweets.nap-17960615-700: I am sending Captain Aymé to Alexandria to command the engineers at the fortress.
tweets.nap-17960615-701: When I learned the Rhine countryside was open, I sent a column toward Lake Como to seize it.
tweets.nap-17960615-703: I have arrested about fifteen bandit leaders accused of murdering our soldiers.
tweets.nap-17960615-704: I have established several batteries along the Genoa coast.
tweets.nap-17960621-702: I am sending you a copy of the requisition I made to the commissioners and the measures they have taken in response.
tweets.nap-17960626-702: I have just learned that an order stopping traffic from Bologna to Florence may have prevented Manfredini from passing.
tweets.nap-17960629-701: I learned that an English frigate seized two French vessels worth half a million pounds just before we entered Livorno.
tweets.nap-17960705-702: I warned the navy minister that commissioners could go to Rome to collect as much as four million in cash.
tweets.nap-17960706-702: I am forwarding the note the Secretary of State gave Faypoult and that he then sent to me.
tweets.nap-17960706-703: I understand why these men are seeking relief by the only means still open to them.
tweets.nap-17960707-701: I trust you will order this as soon as you can.
tweets.nap-17960709-700: I need them to receive a special supply of machine guns.
tweets.nap-17960714-700: I am sending two deputies from Ferrara’s Legion to meet with you.
tweets.nap-17960714-701: I am sending you a copy of my letter to Miot, who has agreed to go to Rome and secure our contributions.
tweets.nap-17960714-702: The Prince of Belmonte-Pignatelli has made the same overtures concerning the Emperor that I reported to you.
tweets.nap-17960728-700: I want the bridge works on the Adige finished as quickly as possible.
tweets.nap-17960729-702: I am waiting for news about General Sauret’s division.
tweets.nap-17960729-703: I am waiting for Berthier and the staff officers to arrive.
tweets.nap-17960730-704: I am placing Augereau behind the Molinella at Gasllaro. He has only half a brigade, so you must reinforce him.
tweets.nap-17960803-700: I am letting you know that we fought a general engagement today.
tweets.nap-17960804-700: I need you to prepare 1,800 rations for the prisoners arriving in Brescia tonight; that will bring the total to 5,800.
tweets.nap-17960804-701: I have sent Masséna’s division from Lonato to join the other attack columns against Wurmser between Castiglione and Mantua.
tweets.nap-17960808-703: I want you to tell me what steps you have taken in response to my request.
tweets.nap-17960811-700: I am sending fifteen mounted men to arrest the priest at Soncino and transfer him to a Milan prison.
tweets.nap-17960811-701: I have ordered supplies for 1,500 men for ten days, with a hundred gunners ready to serve the fortress artillery.
tweets.nap-17960812-703: I am sending you several copies of the report you requested.
tweets.nap-17960812-705: I have learned that former Jesuits, priests, and religious orders are disturbing public peace.
tweets.nap-17960812-706: I had heard you were ill in Milan, so I temporarily put Dubois in charge of the army’s cavalry. I want you to know why.
tweets.nap-17960813-700: I am told that the company must take responsibility for the 400,000 pounds.
tweets.nap-17960813-702: I am carrying out the chief general’s instructions.
tweets.nap-17960813-703: I am letting you know Sauret’s division is at Lodrone with about five thousand men.
tweets.nap-17960813-704: I have received your account of the movements and the position you now hold.
tweets.nap-17960818-702: We need much more biscuit, especially at Verona, Brescia, and Peschiera, and we need transport to move it.
tweets.nap-17960819-701: I have received your note asking about French troop movements in the Grand Duke’s territory. I will keep you informed.
tweets.nap-17960821-700: I order you to go at once to Storo and take command of Sauret’s division.
tweets.nap-17960909-700: We move to this position tomorrow.
tweets.nap-17960912-700: I authorize you to use Milan’s civic guard as an escort while you evacuate the prisoners in groups of five hundred.
tweets.nap-17960913-701: I want all your troops ready to attack tomorrow, following the orders you will receive.
tweets.nap-17960924-702: I have attached an order for 25,000 pounds to cover the expenses you disputed.
tweets.nap-17960924-703: I had already authorized a payment of 20,000 pounds to Faultrier.
tweets.nap-17960926-701: I want the priest Zerbi, whom I ordered arrested, released.
tweets.nap-17960927-700: The enemy is still far from your walls, but war may bring a siege at any moment. I am planning for that possibility.
tweets.nap-17960930-700: I want Willot to requisition National Guard detachments from citizens committed to the Republic and public order.
tweets.nap-17960930-702: I want a defensive enclosure built quickly at Borgoforte, with shelter for 1,500 men.
tweets.nap-17961002-701: Help us as quickly as you can if you want me to keep sending you 700,000 francs.
tweets.nap-17961003-700: I am asking you to send every wounded serviceman to Lyon, where they can receive care.
tweets.nap-17961006-700: I am sending Your Holiness a manifesto circulating in Rome. Please tell me whether it is official or an enemy publication.
tweets.nap-17961006-701: I want the commissioner arrested and brought to Milan, wherever he is found.
tweets.nap-17961008-701: I am sending you the proclamation concerning Modena.
tweets.nap-17961012-700: We have lived on requisitions for too long. I want that practice brought under control.
tweets.nap-17961012-702: I am sending you a letter for the congregation. Use it to secure the legion’s prompt release.
tweets.nap-17961017-700: I found 64,000 pounds belonging to the King of Spain at Livorno. I took 20,000 for the army.
tweets.nap-17961017-701: I thought the Lombards were Italy’s most patriotic people. Bologna, Ferrara, Reggio, and Modena are now proving even more energetic.
tweets.nap-17961019-700: I want his papers sealed and him sent away under safe escort.
tweets.nap-17961025-700: As the Republic’s chief representative in Lombardy, I charge you with ending abuses and putting matters right.
tweets.nap-17961027-700: I ask you to accept the assurances of my esteem and consideration.
tweets.nap-17961028-700: I am forwarding a passage I have just received from the Executive Board.
tweets.nap-17961102-703: I have ordered the seventy-fifth Demi-Brigade, three thousand strong, to be at Montebello tomorrow.
tweets.nap-17961103-700: I want you to report what steps you have taken on this matter.
tweets.nap-17961114-700: The Austrians have suffered heavily. I hope we can defeat them completely at our next encounter.
tweets.nap-17961119-700: I hoped to reach Villanova in the morning, seize the enemy’s artillery and baggage, and strike the army from the flank and rear.
tweets.nap-17961119-702: You have lost a husband dear to you; I have lost a friend to whom I was deeply attached.
tweets.nap-17961120-700: I am forwarding a letter I received from the French Republic’s consul in Livorno.
tweets.nap-17961122-700: I have ordered Joubert to drive the Austrians from the Chiusa fort at once if it is not already ours.
tweets.nap-17961123-702: I received the letter you sent me from Miot.
tweets.nap-17961124-700: We took Rivoli and the Corona, then pursued the enemy as far as Preabocco.
tweets.nap-17961205-700: I have received your letter announcing the peace just concluded in Paris.
tweets.nap-17961210-700: I have sent you instructions on how to deal with the Garfagnana. Follow them carefully.
tweets.nap-17961210-701: I have received your letter and the note enclosed with it.
tweets.nap-17961213-700: I expect you to pay one million francs toward the army’s expenses. I have already drawn bills on you for 1,000 francs.
tweets.nap-17961218-700: I want you to wear the insignia of your new rank and tell me which officer you chose as your second aide-de-camp.
tweets.nap-17961220-700: I need the postmaster at Castelluccio to keep fifteen horses in his stable. Take whatever steps will make that happen.
tweets.nap-17961226-700: I think we should send a dozen workers to clear the blinds as well.
tweets.nap-17961228-701: I believe we can agree on Mantua’s status, but carrying it out will remain impossible.
tweets.nap-17961228-703: I am sending you a copy of the letter I wrote to the Executive Board, as you requested.
tweets.nap-17961228-704: I have asked the Executive Board to consider her request. I ask you to support it.
tweets.nap-17961228-706: I want Cartier warned that he is removed from his post for abandoning his unit during his absence.
tweets.nap-17961231-700: I want you to send me an update once all your work is permanently in place, in the same format as before.
tweets.nap-17970105-700: I have appointed Trivulzi to command Milan’s National Guard. Inform Kilmaine and the Lombard administration.
tweets.nap-17970113-701: The enemy has broken through near Verona with about six thousand men. I have ordered an immediate attack.
tweets.nap-17970115-700: We captured six thousand prisoners, six cannon, and several flags from the enemy.
tweets.nap-17970115-701: I need you to send enough food to Saint-Georges to let the post hold out for two days.
tweets.nap-17970126-701: I want you to tell the chief general what you think about this.
tweets.nap-17970202-700: I want you to keep the relay posts supplied so the horses remain available for the mail service.
tweets.nap-17970217-700: I expect you have received the Eleventh Demi-Brigade. The Twenty-sixth Light Infantry should already be at Verona.
tweets.nap-17970218-701: I am confident you will recognize this general’s exceptional service to the Republic and his commitment to our government and constitution.
tweets.nap-17970225-701: I am deeply troubled by the Bologna Civic Guard’s irregular and seditious conduct.
tweets.nap-17970225-702: I need you to gather these documents and summarize them; I have no time to read them all.
tweets.nap-17970304-700: I need you to explain under whose orders troops are being sent through Mantua.
tweets.nap-17970310-700: I want your division moving toward Feltre so you can attack early tomorrow if the enemy is there in strength.
tweets.nap-17970313-703: I expect Bernadotte’s division to reach Conegliano tomorrow and join us as we attack the enemy.
tweets.nap-17970324-700: I am sending you sixteen horses for your artillery.
tweets.nap-17970328-701: I will protect your religion, your people, your property, and your customs.

tweets.nap-18030711-701: I approve of how you handled Jourdan’s communications with London, unless we discover he is deceiving us.
tweets.nap-18030711-703: I want them stopped at the border so we can identify them and keep them out of the Vendée.
tweets.nap-18030715-702: I find the ceremony you sent for the bishops incompatible with our present customs.
tweets.nap-18030720-702: I want you to work with the Italians and accelerate the conscription.
tweets.nap-18030723-700: I have received your letters, Citizen Consul.
tweets.nap-18030724-700: I will make this journey on another occasion.
tweets.nap-18030726-700: All the Belgian ladies were presented to my wife today.
tweets.nap-18030726-702: I think communes should be told that anyone buying military equipment will be exempt from billeting troops.
tweets.nap-18030729-701: I am sending you the forest administration’s report.
tweets.nap-18030808-700: I reached Sedan this morning and decided to go to Reims after repeated requests from the city.
tweets.nap-18030808-702: I have read with interest the new reports on the Irish insurrection.
tweets.nap-18030808-704: I am prepared to offer them twenty-five thousand men, forty thousand rifles, and all necessary artillery and ammunition.
tweets.nap-18030809-700: I hear from every direction that our ships are returning toward Spain and the northern coast.
tweets.nap-18030810-700: I am receiving complaints that payment orders are not being honoured.
tweets.nap-18030813-700: I want you to inform the Swedish minister of the order you have issued.
tweets.nap-18030813-701: I am sending you the decisions concerning the Swiss capitulation.
tweets.nap-18030823-700: I am returning the papers with my comments and notes for a reply to the Russian cabinet.
tweets.nap-18030823-701: I accept the numbers assigned to the different buildings.
tweets.nap-18030912-701: I am surprised that we have received no further news.
tweets.nap-18030918-702: I want you to tell me when they will arrive so I can issue new orders.
tweets.nap-17960504-702: I have ordered Augereau’s division to occupy Pizzale, Cervesina, and nearby villages along the Po. Have bread prepared ahead for the troops.
tweets.nap-17960504-703: I have ordered Masséna to hold his positions, move captured oats to Tortona, and watch the floating bridges being built opposite Sale.
tweets.nap-17960504-705: I have ordered four hundred prisoners brought for exchange for the four hundred you sent to Cherasco. My chief of staff will send the list of your captured officers.
